# AI NPC Cyberpunk Mod: TODO and captain's log

The single working document for development: open items first, then a dated log, then the standing facts every session needs. It replaces `HANDOFF_README.md` (removed October 5; still in git history). Earlier code and docs were written by a weaker model, so verify claims against code and data before relying on them.

The log entry "2026-10-15 (TODO cleanup)" lists what was removed or merged; the older "2026-10-14 (TODO cleanup)" entry keeps the long text of the shortened live-check lists. Log entries that say "NOT merged" or "NOT installed" predate the merges: every branch is in `main` except `skippy-stock`, `skippy-voice`, `v-voice-finetune` (not used) and `youtube-home-2` (superseded when YouTube was removed). Every 2026-10-17 branch (spawned characters, companion items 1 to 6, group count and look-ahead, pre-open, Voxtral retry, V's voice engine, Bonsai lite) is in `main` 07541c71, pushed and in the rebuilt v0.2 release.

Install state: everything on `main` 07541c71 is installed in the game (2026-10-17, with `dev_install_tree.py`), including the reds and the archives. `mod/diagnostics.lua` is the uncommitted dev copy and is never installed. ### Release schedule (decided 2026-10-10)
- **Main mod on Nexus: Sun 18 Oct 2026, about 11:00 UTC (16:30 IST), version 0.2** (tag `v0.2`; scheme 0.N, hotfix 0.N.M). It lands two days before *Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2* (all 10 episodes on Netflix Tue 20 Oct, about 07:00 UTC). Release-blocking bugs must be fixed by then.
- **Add-on 1, Skippy: Tue 20 Oct. Add-on 2, Delamain: Sun 25 Oct, about 11:00 UTC.** Separate Nexus pages that require the main mod. Each lives in its own private repository (`alystria-ai/cyberpunk-convai-skippy`, `-delamain`; sibling folders of this checkout) with its own zip from `tools/build.mjs`. The add-on API stays here (`docs/ADDON_API.md`, `bridge/addons*.mjs`, `mod/addons.lua`, `addons/example/`).
- Shared plan: 100 turns per player per local day, 12 a minute (`DAILY_LIMIT` in `bridge/shared-key-guard.mjs`; the backend sets the limit, README "Changing the daily limit"; `docs/OWN_CONVAI_KEY.md`, "Daily limit on the shared plan"). Raise it if usage allows.
- Timing facts: about 35 new Cyberpunk mods a day, so a new one stays on page 1 of New for 12 to 14 hours; trending ranks mods first published in its window by endorsements; Steam peaks about 13:00 to 14:00 UTC and Sundays run 10 to 20% above weekdays.

**2026-10-19: uniform MCM rows, Relationships as a submenu (branch `fix/mcm-uniform-rows` from main 8077fa2a, worktree `wt-mcm-uniform`, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT seen in the game).** From the user's screenshots (setting rows indented and purple, action rows and read-only lines flush left, read-only lines bigger). Read in MCM 0.10.5's source, public API only. **Purple** is decided by `mcm_model.lua` `settingDisplay` / `settingDefaultState` (1090-1103): a row is "modified" only when it has a readable default (`defaultValue` plus `capabilities.reset ~= false`, `catalog.lua` `normalizeDefaultCapabilities` 118-141, `defaults.lua` `has`/`isDefault`) and its value differs; `highlighted` then colours the label (`MCMPanelContent.reds` `McmUiAddManagedLabel`, `McmUiColorModified`). Our rows no longer carry a default (`mod/mcm-host.lua` `convert`, `reset = false`), so nothing is purple. Lost with it: MCM's Defaults footer button (`bottomActions`, only when something resettable is off its default) and the Modified (n) counter and its filter (`modifiedSettingCount` needs defaults). Replaced by our own **Restore defaults** footer action on Settings and Relationships (id `defaults:restore`, beside Back): applies `manager-ui.lua` `M.defaults()` (now covers both pages) through `M.apply`, pressed twice (MCM's public API has no confirmation for an action: the first press relabels the button "Press again to restore" and says so on the status line; any other button or page drops it); MCM refuses it while drafts are pending, like every action. **Indent** is not removable: a setting's label sits at `contentLabelX` = marker x 20 + marker width 20 + gap 8 = 48 (`MCMLayout.reds` 340-344), a constant used by `McmUiAddManagedLabel` for every switch, list, slider and key row, whether or not there is a default or a marker; no presentation option (`locale`, `descriptionFontSize`, `rowFontSize`, `labelWidthFraction`, `statusPlacement`, `quietActions`) or row property moves it. Actions (`McmUiAddActionSetting`) and read-only lines (`McmUiAddReadonly`) are hard-coded at x 20. There is no public way to make the actions and lines match the settings, so two alignments remain on the Settings page: x 48 for switches, lists and sliders, x 20 for buttons and status lines. **Read-only font**: `McmUiAddReadonly` builds its label with `McmUiCreateAction` (`MCMPanelActions.reds` 477-489), font 26, value on the right at 22; `rowFontSize` is meant to reach it (`MCMPanelPresentation.Walk`, run by `McmUiFinalizePagePresentation`) but did not in the live check. Voice status and Johnny's standing (the only read-only lines of the Settings page) are now drawn as status buttons: an action (`McmUiAddActionSetting`: label size 22 at x 20 like Memory and the key rows, the value as the button's text on the right); pressing one does nothing (its help is on hover). Other pages (Memory, Help, party lines) keep MCM's read-only lines at size 26. If the in-game look of a status button is worse than the old line, the one-line switch is the `core.view() == 'settings'` branch in `convert`. **Relationships** is a page of its own in `mod/manager-ui.lua` (view `relationships`, back to Settings, `relationshipRows`), opened by a Relationships row (Open) beside Memory in Conversations; both hosts get it (NSUI tab and MCM). `M.defaults()` covers both pages and rebuilds the page on screen afterwards. Tests: `bridge/mcm-host.test.mjs` (new: no purple at any time, Settings page uniform in size and colour with exactly the two MCM columns, status buttons, Restore defaults two-press flow and refusal with drafts, Relationships page; layout check of every page includes Relationships), `bridge/mcm-fake.mjs` (layout now reports MCM's own Defaults button and Modified counter from the rules above), `bridge/nsui-manager.test.mjs` (Relationships page walk, Restore defaults on it), `bridge/manager.test.mjs`. **Asks for MCM's author (Antrix offered API functions):** a presentation option for the setting label column (for example `markerColumn = false` or a `labelIndent`, so switches, lists and sliders start at x 20 like buttons), a per-mod switch for the changed-colour mark that does not need dropping defaults (so Defaults and Modified (n) stay), one font size for read-only lines (`McmUiAddReadonly` label 26 vs rowFontSize 22), and a confirmation step for an action result (for example `requiresConfirmation`). Recheck in the game: Settings page (nothing purple; status buttons size and look; the footer shows Restore defaults beside Back), Restore defaults twice (values back, Local AI model, Mature content rule), Relationships button and page, Back and Escape from it, Apply on a Relationships list, the NSUI tab's Relationships page.

**2026-10-19 (V's voice grace; branch `fix/v-voice-typed` from main `fe698464`; committed, NOT pushed, NOT merged).** Live finding in Silent power mode (V on Pocket, companions Voxtral): V's typed line was dropped, `reason=slower-than-reply`, V's first PCM at 3006 ms against the reply's first frame at 3053 ms. **Root cause:** V's line did start at the top of the turn (36 ms in; the 1340 ms `voiceStart` in the report is the companion's clock), but the first Pocket line of a session pays the voice's preparation (about 2.8 s of the 3 s) because the composer warm-up prepared nothing while V's gender was unknown (two clips, no line yet) and a still-loading worker prepared nothing either; and `VLine.holds()` dropped a line that was 40 ms from audible on the first ask. **Fix** (`bridge/v-voice.mjs`, `v-helper-voice.mjs`, `voice-selection.mjs`, `convai-bridge.mjs`): (1) V's gender is remembered in `v-voice-gender.json` (state folder) and the voice is prepared on the first composer open of a session; with nothing known both are prepared in turn and the second is skipped once a line says which V it is; (2) V's own Pocket worker prepares V's voice as soon as it has loaded (`onVHelperReady`, no renderer page opened); (3) a 600 ms grace (`V_GRACE_MS`, `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_V_GRACE_MS`, 0 = old rule) instead of the instant drop, capped by a 4 s rescue budget (`V_RESCUE_BUDGET_MS`: wait plus the line's estimated length, so a long late line is dropped at once); (4) `[VVoice] this session: N typed line(s) spoken, M not heard (reason=count), K not started (reason=count)` on the first line and every drop, and typed lines that could not start are counted by reason, so a support report shows how often V was heard. Stage-clock numbers (`scripts/Measure-VVoice.mjs`, simulated): warm V audible at 323 ms, reply +265 ms; slow CPU 1500 ms, reply +1514; cold 2800 ms, old rule drops V (reply +2), grace rescues it but the reply then follows V's line (+2824), which is why the warm voice is the real fix and the budget exists. Tests: `bridge/v-voice.test.mjs` (grace, budget, totals, remembered gender, warm order), `bridge/v-helper-voice.test.mjs` (the ready hook). Docs: `docs/V_VOICE.md` (new section), README (two places). **Decision for the user:** the grace trades up to about 2.5 s of extra reply latency on a rare late turn for hearing V; `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_V_GRACE_MS=0` restores the old drop. Not done: the 200 ms between V's `playStart` and `ttsSent` (event loop busy on a slow CPU); the shared Pocket worker (Pocket companions) is prepared on composer open only, not at load.

**2026-10-19 (Local AI timeout letter; branch `fix/local-ai-mature-timeout` from main 676dcfcf, then main 9fb7e79c and edb10e55 merged in (custom provider and its reasoning handling, Native Settings UI, packs overlap, first-turn provider with the no-reply reasons: a local failure arrives first and keeps `local-failed` and its reason, so the game shows that or the 90 s reading of the bridge status, never both), NOT merged into main, NOT installed; every `bridge/` change needs a bridge restart, `mod/init.lua` a CET reload).** The letter: Local AI preheats and loads, Mature content on, "Gemma 4 E4B", all 0.2.1, manual install, every reply times out (the game's log: `Conversation timed out`). **Not reproduced and the player's cause is unknown (no report came with it).** On the dev machine (RTX 4080 Laptop) the bridge's own flow (`LocalLlmServer` with its real arguments, then `TextProviderHost` turns with the Mature layer) answers every turn with the Mature good model (`Gemma4-E4B-MiniFantasy-V1-Q4_K_M.gguf`: first word 1.2 s cold on a 4,800-token prompt, 0.23 s warm, 34 to 75 tokens/s), with the normal Gemma 4 E4B plus the Mature layer and with the Mature lite Qwen3.5-4B; every reply ends with `finish_reason: stop`. GGUF headers read without loading: both Gemma files are `gemma4`, bos 2, eos 1, no eot key (llama.cpp ends a turn on `<turn|>` 106 by itself); templates 16,804 chars (Mature, the older Gemma 4 one) and 18,567 (normal, the 2026-07-09 canonical one) render a plain chat alike; the Qwen template opens with `<think>` unless `enable_thinking` is false (`--reasoning off` sets it). Ranked causes: (1) the bridge's local limits (90 s first word, 90 s total, a retry after a timeout, no stall limit, an unbounded wait for a model that is loading: `text-provider-host.mjs` 118 to 128 before the change) were not shorter than the game's own 90 s (`mod/init.lua` 3951), so any stall ended as the same silent timeout with a generic notice (3959) and no log line said why; (2) a turn sent while the model loads or reloads (first start, a first-time warm-up of up to 3 x 240 s, a reload after the choice changed) waited past 90 s; (3) 0.2.1's first start of a launch ignored the saved model and Mature content (already fixed on main by `20fa585c`, so the player's "Gemma 4 E4B" was most likely the normal model); (4) machine-specific slowness the log could not show: a card shared with the game and OmniVoice, short system memory (Gemma 4 E4B keeps 2.8 GB of per-layer tables in system memory, mapped from the file), or the wrong adapter (an AMD APU reports as much memory as the system and could win the most-memory pick over a laptop's card). Fixed in the three commits: the local turn has an 80 s budget; a request is cut after 60 s with no stream event or 25 s of silence (llama-server's `return_progress` makes a slow prompt count as life); no retry of a timeout; a model still loading ends the turn at once and the load goes on; a model that only thinks is stopped after 160 pieces; our own server gets stop strings and `enable_thinking: false`; a reply ends at the first end-of-turn marker; every failure has a reason, a record of what came when and one plain sentence, which the game shows after its `local-failed` sentence (`errorDetail`); the bridge log gets `[local] model ready: ...` (file, family, chat template source/length/hash, eos, build, device, context, system memory, load and warm-up time), `[local] graphics devices: ...`, `[LocalTurn] FAILED ...` and the first turn per load, and the last ten lines of a server that did not start or stopped; `runtime/mistral-state.json` carries `localDiagnostics` and the support report copies it as `localAi.diagnostics`; an AMD APU is a last resort in the device pick. Changed at the user's request: the chat model now loads at normal priority and is lowered to below normal once it is ready (after the warm-up); generation stays at below normal for the frame rate (`docs/LOCAL_AI.md`, 'A machine with no CPU to spare'). The Nexus reporter's second letter (RTX 5070 Ti, both packs, Mature off shows one model 'the Uncensored one', no warm-up notice, no reply; Mature on shows 'No reply received'): with both packs in place the list has both models (tested), so the Local AI pack's marker or model file was not in the folder; Mature off then cannot start Local AI (`mature-off`), hence no warm-up; the model row's help now names a model whose file is missing (`describePackFiles`, `packFileProblems`) and the support report has `localAi.packFiles` (markers, named files with sizes, the .gguf files of `models/`). Not changed: a pin of `standard` loads the normal Gemma 4 even with Mature on and the pack installed (the settings page selects the uncensored model when Mature is turned on). **2026-10-19: MO2 compatibility, step 3: the player's settings and phone chats survive a launch under Mod Organizer 2 (branch `fix/mo2-step3`, from main 120bc54f, worktree `wt-mo2-step3`, code commit 0e0ea540, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game or on MO2; Lua needs a CET reload and the Runtime files a bridge restart).** Step 2's open decision is closed with its option 2: nothing is shipped for the state files; the service keeps a durable copy and writes it back before the Lua reads it.
- **Design.** `bridge/game-state.mjs` (new). The copies live in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AiNpcCyberpunkMod\data\game-state\`: `settings.json` and `phone-history.json` (each with `.previous`), `memory-chat-resets.json`, `witness-receipts.json`, `decision-ledger.json`, `addon-settings.json`, `npc-names.json` (`GAME_STATE_FILES`, a test keeps it equal to the manifest's `state` class). **Start** (`start-service.mjs`, the first thing after the layout is known, before the legacy carry-over, the data move and `prepareState`; only with a data home): per file, a real non-empty file always wins and refreshes the copy (a copy more than 2 s newer than the older real file it replaces is kept in `game-state/older/`, one slot a file); a missing or empty file gets the copy written into it in place; JSON that does not parse is neither copied nor restored; a start with nothing to do is two stats a file, and a read only when size or time differ (a copy carries its file's time). Then `runtime/state-restore.json` (`{version, state: "done", written, restored, refreshed, errors}`, a new empty exchange placeholder in the Scripts zip). **Running** (`GameStateSync`, in the bridge): a stat of each file on the existing 500 ms settings poll plus a directory-watcher wake a few ms after a save (`file-wake.mjs`, new `mergeHandlers` because `addon-settings.json` is also an add-on watch), a copy only when a file changed and is non-empty JSON, a final pass at shutdown; it never fills a file in and never deletes a main file's copy. On only when the launcher sets `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_GAME_STATE` (with a data home), so development and tests are unchanged.
- **Startup order (the finding).** The RED4ext plugin starts the service at process start; CET loads the mod only after the engine and its scripts are up, so the restore (a Node process that has just started, a few stats and writes) should nearly always be first. **Not measured**, so the Lua does not rely on it. New `mod/state-restore.lua` (global `convaiStateRestore`, set at the top of `init.lua`): a reader that finds its file missing or empty asks `waiting()`; true until a signal written after this game session began (`os.time() - os.clock()`, because the shipped empty placeholder is modified in place and last session's signal is still there at the next launch) or 120 s after the first question (older Runtime, no service). Held back, never overwriting: `manager.lua` keeps the defaults in memory (`settingsDeferred`), `saveSettings` refuses, the next `loadSettings` after the restore reads the file and `initialize` pushes the restored voice, subtitle and enabled values again; `phone-chat.lua` binds no world and saves nothing until the restore is over (`storePending`, `storeReady`, 10 Hz tick) and then reads the file again; `addons.lua` registers with defaults, refuses to write and merges the saved values in afterwards; `npc-names.lua` makes a vendor name without keeping it. A file that is there is never waited for (a test counts the questions: 0), the module is asked at most once a second while waiting, and nothing runs per frame beyond a boolean test in code that already ran. The `os.clock` assumption is MSVC's wall time since process start; if CET's `os.clock` were CPU time, a fresh install (no file) would hold defaults for up to 120 s, and a restored file would still be read at once.
- **npc-names.json.** In the state set, and moved from next to `init.lua` (a new file in the mod folder's root under MO2) to `runtime/npc-names.json`; a store an earlier version saved next to `init.lua` is read until one exists in `runtime/` (`docs/NPC_NAMES.md` updated).
- **Behaviour change for normal installs.** Besides the extra copy, a state file that is deleted by hand to reset it comes back at the next start (a missing file is what MO2 leaves behind, so the two cannot be told apart): delete the same file in `data\game-state\` too. Documented in `docs/PACKAGING.md`.
- **Packages.** Scripts: `mod/state-restore.lua` (new), `init.lua`, `manager.lua`, `phone-chat.lua`, `addons.lua`, `npc-names.lua`, `runtime/state-restore.json` (empty). Runtime: `bridge/game-state.mjs` (new, in `BRIDGE_MODULES` and the release plan), `bridge/file-wake.mjs`, `bridge/convai-bridge.mjs`, `packaging/runtime/start-service.mjs`, `packaging/runtime/prepare-state.mjs`. Scripts new with Runtime old: no signal, so only a first-ever launch (no file) holds the defaults for 120 s. Runtime new with Scripts old: the restore works; an old Lua that read first could save defaults, and that real file then wins (the copy it replaces goes to `older/`). The development install list (`scripts/development-files.json`) has the new Lua file.
- **Tests.** New `bridge/game-state.test.mjs` (17: restore order, newer wins in both directions, empty files restored in place, unreadable JSON, the sync, flush, one stat a file), `packaging/game-state-restore.test.mjs` (6: the launcher end to end, before the slow work, the signal, the environment variable), `bridge/state-restore-lua.test.mjs` (18: the module, `settings.json` missing or empty, nothing written while held back, the restored file used, first start, no service, 0 questions on an ordinary start, phone chats, add-on settings), four cases in `bridge/npc-names.test.mjs`. Every guard was mutation-checked (removing it fails a test). Full `npm test` (6,167 tests) twice. First run: 6,125 pass, 24 skipped, 17 todo-marked (the known BUG boundary tests) and one real failure, a source-text check in `bridge/setup-check.test.mjs` that wants `void setupCheck.run` straight after `await pollSettings(false)`, which my first-poll line had separated (fixed by moving the line). Final run after the fix: 6,123 pass and 3 fail, all timing tests that fail only under the load of the whole suite and pass alone (`bridge/local-llm-server.test.mjs` "a changed choice reloads the model", `bridge/setup-check.test.mjs` "one run at a time", `packaging/place-packs.test.mjs` "nothing to fix: ... well under 50 ms"; 79 tests in those three files pass when run on their own, and 317 related tests pass). The known 'native install quarantines' failure did not appear (the game was not running). The worktree has a junction to the main checkout's node_modules and no dev `runtime/` data.
- **Not covered.** The Lua's temp-file, backup and swap protocol for these files is unchanged; how USVFS treats that swap on a file that lives in Overwrite is unproven, and the copy follows whatever ends up on disk. A service that starts more than 120 s after the Lua gave up finds the defaults it saved, and that real file wins (the copy goes to `older/`). Two installs on one Windows account share `game-state/` as they share `data/`. Values other modules cached before a late restore (the story-talk setting handed to the face service in `onInit`) are not pushed again.
- **Live checks owed.** MO2: install Scripts and Runtime physically, start from MO2, change a voice option and send one phone message, quit; start again: the option and the chat are there, `bridge-service.log` has `Player state in runtime/: ... restored (...)`, Overwrite holds only CET's log and the state files; look at `game-state/`. Normal install: the same steps change nothing for the player; `game-state/` holds the copies and `runtime/state-restore.json` has a recent `written`. Also worth one look: the timing of the restore against the first settings read (the order was reasoned, not measured), and a start with `settings.json` deleted by hand (the copy comes back).

**2026-10-19 (branch `fix/mo2-virtual-runtime`, from main 5375b29f, 2 commits; NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game): a player's service never started with the Scripts and the Runtime both installed as MO2 mods (Ultraviolence modlist), and nothing said why; a start can no longer end without a word.** Report: `deliverables/player-reports/discord-ultraviolence-mo2/convai-report-lua.txt`. MCM and the CET bindings work; `runtime/bridge-service.json` stays the launcher's `starting` / `launcher-started` (supervisorPid 12584, written 03:12:06Z) five minutes later; `bridge-status`, `knowledge-status` and `local-voice-state` read "not available"; every talk ends in "Conversation service unavailable: stopped". The player's Runtime is 0.2.1, whose `start-service.mjs` still ended silently when the data folder could not be made or the supervisor could not be imported. No service log, `launcher.log` or `bridge.stderr.log` was sent.
- **What was found (no cause can be proven without those logs).** Nothing on the start path resolves a link or compares a resolved path with the game root: `packaging/runtime-layout.mjs` (`realpath`, "cannot redirect into another location") belongs to the bootstrap route that `launcher.ini` never starts, and the voice workers' `realpathSync.native` comparisons (`pocket-voice.mjs`, `phone-analysis-config.mjs`, `resident-voice.mjs`) canonicalize both sides alike and run after the bridge is up. Ranked: (1) the process ends or hangs before its first status and nothing says so (`start-service.mjs` of 0.2.1: unguarded `mkdirSync` of the data folder and unguarded supervisor import; static imports; `publishFailure` swallows its own write error; the supervisor writes nothing before it holds `bridge-supervisor.lock`, `bridge-supervisor.mjs` `run()`/`acquireLock()`); (2) `node.exe` runs outside USVFS or sees another tree: the launcher saw `init.lua` through the game's hooks (`CyberpunkConvaiLauncher.c:221`), the service never checked, and its writes land in the physical game folder, shadowed by the Scripts mod's placeholders (fits `bridge-status` "not available"); (3) a supervisor waiting for the lock of a session that never ended; (4) the process crashing at once (the launcher closes the process handle, `:345`, so an immediate exit is invisible). The launcher's "starting" was also read as "not running, restart the game" (`service-status.lua`), with no code.
- **Built.** Runtime: `start-service.mjs` writes its own `starting` / `service-starting` in place from the first line (`source: "service"`, `stage`, a `view` such as `usvfs no; Runtime outside the game folder; init.lua visible` that the short report prints, refreshed every 5 s for at most 5 minutes), loads its own modules inside a guard, ends an uncaught error in `failed` with a short path-free `reason` (`install-incomplete`, `service-error`), logs a `View:` line (usvfs loaded or not, the Runtime inside or outside the game folder, `init.lua` and `runtime/` visible) and, when it cannot see the CET mod's `init.lua`, stops before writing anything under the game folder (`game-folder-not-visible`, exit 3). `bridge-supervisor.mjs` publishes `starting` / `waiting-for-previous-service` after 5 s of waiting for the lock (heartbeat kept), and a status can carry a `reason`. Scripts: `service-status.lua` reads a launcher or start-script `starting` that nothing refreshed as coming up for 90 s and as a service that never came up after that (kind `failed`, code `service-silent`); the notice, a blocked talk, `lostSince` and the Help row end with the status's own words in English, `(service-silent after launcher-started)`, `(install-incomplete at loading-modules: ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: ...)`; `support-report.lua` heads the short report with `PROBLEM: the conversation service did not come up (...)` and where the logs are. No new locale string (the words are appended to the existing sentence); `localization/en.json` regenerated for line numbers only. The Scripts part works with today's 0.2.1 Runtime; the Runtime part needs a Runtime update. Docs: `docs/PACKAGING.md` "Mod Organizer 2: the Runtime as a mod folder".
- **Tests.** `packaging/virtual-runtime.test.mjs` (9: a Runtime in an MO2-style mod folder far from the game prepares and leaves its folder untouched; layout; place-packs never takes it for a misplaced pack; a missing module, an uncaught error and a hung stage each end with a status; the not-visible stop writes nothing in the game folder; a physical install), `bridge/supervisor-lock-status.test.mjs` (4), new cases in `service-status` and `support-report-lua`; all of them fail on main. Full suite on the branch: 6419 tests, 6395 pass, 0 fail, 24 skipped (an earlier run under heavy machine load failed `group-lookahead-bridge` and `mistral-rate` on timing; both pass alone and in the final run). Step 3 (`fix/mo2-step3`) auto-merges with it (only `docs/PACKAGING.md` conflicts, two appended sections); in the merged tree the not-visible check runs before step 3's restore block, and 87 tests of both pass. Merge this branch first: step 3 only helps once the service starts.

**2026-10-19 (branch `fix/reds-safety`, from main 5375b29f; NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game): the scripts no longer break the whole redscript compile when a requirement is missing.** Two players reported the redscript popup right after installing 0.2.1 (compile failed, naming this mod; the game then runs with no scripts at all, other mods' too) and "nothing in MCM". No logs yet; the likely cause is a missing or old Codeware or Audioware. Compiled offline with redscript's `scc` (0.5.31, from `ref mods/`) against the game's `final.redscripts`, the four requirement mods' scripts copied from the install: **before**, all present OK; Audioware removed FAILED (Speech.reds, this mod alone); Codeware removed FAILED (this mod in 7 files, plus Audioware and MCM, which need Codeware themselves); MCM removed OK; a fresh install with none of Codeware, Audioware, MCM, TweakXL FAILED (this mod alone, 8 files). **After**, all five OK, except Codeware removed, which still fails but only in Audioware and MCM (this mod 0 files); with Codeware, Audioware, MCM and TweakXL all removed the compile succeeds. Also compiled with a Codeware without its UI modules (this mod clean) and with the requirement scripts listed after ours, as in the game (guards still on). Output sizes: all present 18,206,626 bytes against 18,205,570 before (the new file).
- **Reds.** `@if(ModuleExists("Codeware"))`, `"Codeware.UI"`, `"Codeware.UI.TextInput"` and `"Audioware"` guard exactly what the compiler flagged, with plain stand-ins for every method Lua calls (false, empty or nothing): `Speech.reds` (Audioware), `Composer.reds` (the text box, `ConvaiOpenComposer` returns false), `Face.reds` and `KnowledgeState.reds` (Codeware: `ScriptableService`, entity callbacks, session callbacks; `ConvaiFaceStatus`/`Request` say `codeware-missing`), `PhoneChat.reds` (a stand-in `ConvaiPhoneChatInput`), `PhoneContacts.reds` (key callbacks moved into `ConvaiStartPhoneKeys`/`ConvaiStopPhoneKeys`, join/leave marks), `Holocall.reds` (the backdrop), `Manager.reds` (the window). New `Requirements.reds`: `PlayerPuppet:ConvaiRequirements()` returns the modules found when it compiled. With every requirement present the guarded code is the old code (a few statements moved into helper methods with the same body). `ModuleExists` is the only predicate redscript 0.5.31 has (`ClassExists` is "unsupported function"; `&&` and `||` work), so a requirement that is installed but too old to have a class (an old Audioware without `DynamicSoundEvent`) still fails the compile and shows in `redscript_rCURRENT.log`.
- **Manager.reds was kept.** README said nothing opens it, true of the window (`ConvaiOpenManager` has no caller), but `ConvaiManagerVoice()` and `ConvaiManagerSubtitles()` (read by `speech.lua`, `subtitles.lua`, `init.lua`) and `SetVoice`/`SetSubtitles` (called by `manager.lua`) live there as the voice and subtitle on/off switches. The packages take every `.reds` but the retired ones, so `Requirements.reds` ships without a list change (`release-plan.json` and `development-files.json` list it).

Install them and restart the game."), Codeware without its UI parts is "too old". CET console and `probe.log` get one English line per problem. `init.lua` installs each hook set through `convaiGuarded`: a hook that names a method of the missing scripts used to raise in `onInit` before `mcm.install`, which is a likely reason for "nothing in MCM". Also guarded: `manager.initialize/update`, the face service lookups, `mcm-entry`, `phone-input` (once a second without the scripts), the phone catalogue failure line (once, was ten file writes a second), no Chat contacts without the text input, `speech.available` false without Audioware, the talk key says Codeware is missing when the text box is refused. **2026-10-19: eight player-facing bugs fixed for 0.2.2 (branch `fixes-0.2.2`, from main 3c6318da, one commit per bug, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game; `mod/manager.lua` needs a CET reload, every `bridge/` change a bridge restart).** Six come from the todo tests of `test-gaps` (8 of its 25 todo tests; they are normal tests now and 17 are left, items 8 to 24 of `deliverables/tests/REPORT.md`), two (Pocket) had no test. (1) **First Local AI start used the wrong model** (Runtime): the poll applied the saved provider before it read Mature content and the saved `localModel`, and the first sync only records the choice. `pollSettings` now reads Mature content and runs `syncLocalModelChoice` before `mistral.setPreference`; the model-list part (card probe, status publish) is `publishLocalModelList`, after the provider, so the first start waits for nothing but the settings read. The old "mature-off, then start again" workaround is gone. (2) **Settings could lose both copies** (Scripts, `mod/manager.lua` `saveSettings`): an unreadable `settings.json` with a good backup now gives way to the backup first (remove it, rename the backup over it), then the ordinary six steps; every step of the eight leaves a good copy. (3) **BOM in settings.json** (Scripts): `readJSON` strips EF BB BF (it serves every file the manager reads). (4) **BOM in `convai-auth.json`** (Runtime): `readAuthSettings` strips it. (5) and (6) **Damaged memory file and damaged character edit file** (Runtime, `memory-store.mjs`, `character-overrides.mjs`): the load remembers files that were read but not usable (not folders, locked or empty files) and logs them; the first save (or reset) of that character moves the old file to `<key>.json.corrupt` (VendorMemory's name; an older copy is replaced) and logs it once; a forget of the character removes the copy; opening still changes nothing on disk. (7) **Pocket never retried** (Runtime, `voice-selection.mjs`): a failed Pocket now has Omni's bounded retry (45 s, 3 min, 10 min, a fourth failure gives up until the player chooses Pocket again; `pocketRetry` published, `[PocketRetry]` log, `fallback.temporary`), due-checked from the 500 ms poll, only with no reply in flight and playback not Off; it clears the failure so the normal start loads Pocket again, and ends when the player picks another voice, a cloud voice or Multilingual, or the service closes. (8) **Cancelling a Pocket preparation killed the worker** (Runtime, `pocket-voice.mjs`): a cancelled preparation gets `prepareCancelMs` (15 s) instead of 2 s, the worker finishes it, answers `cancelled` and goes on; a cancelled stream keeps 2 s. Not changed: V's own helper Pocket worker (beside OmniVoice) still stays off after a failure until the setting or voice changes (documented design); a cold preparation inside a stream request (after a cache eviction) cancelled in its first 4.5 s can still stop the worker.

**2026-10-19: second round on the NCA seats: the 21:05Z live check failed (branch `fix/nca-seats-2`, from main 9273275d, NOT merged; Lua only: `mod/companion-vehicles.lua`, `mod/companion-vehicle-native.lua`, `mod/companions.lua`, CET reload).** Setup: our Alex plus NCA's Lucy, Rita and Judy, all spawned with `NCA:ForceSpawnCharacter`; the user saw all of them overlap in the passenger seat and Alex and Judy still in the car after V got out. `probe.log` had no vehicle line (the fleet logged nothing), so the first round could not be read; the spawned-character service did see the three followers 8 to 10 m away.
- **Why the first fix counted nobody (most likely).** It read the service with `rawget(_G, 'convaiSpawnedCharacters')`; a module's `_G` in CET need not be the environment init.lua assigns its globals in (`convaiTeleportLog` read the same way has never written a line). The bare global read replaces it. Not proven, the new log will show.
- **Debug-spawned followers are not in NCA's squad** (`ForceSpawnCharacter` calls `NpcManager.Spawn`; only the join path adds to the squad that `EnterVehicle` seats), so NCA has no seat plan for them: its follow behaviour gives each the engine's follower role and the engine's follower AI mounts them, seat by seat as it likes. Their overlapping each other is NCA's and the engine's. Our own copies carry the same role, so the engine can seat Alex too.
- **Fixes (ours).** (1) The count also takes followers by `IsPlayerCompanion`, and returns a report of who it saw and why each was or was not counted. (2) The plan is no longer trusted alone: while a counted rider is still on foot, our companions send no mount, spawn no overflow car and choose no seat for good (poll twice a second, at most 12 s); then the seat comes from the real occupancy. (3) A companion the engine seated in V's car while the fleet planned another car for her is adopted where she sits. (4) Exit: a person in a fleet car other than her planned one is unmounted from the car she is in (before, `leave` waited for ever for a "foreign vehicle" that was V's own car; a seat denied by the first version's plan could have produced exactly that for Alex), and three refused unmounts are retried in rounds ten seconds apart, three rounds at most (before: `exit-failed` for good). (5) New probe lines: `Companion recovery vehicle-boarding` (riders counted, who was seen and why not counted, seats held, the seat for each of our companions, whether it waits), `vehicle-seat`, `vehicle-settled`, `vehicle-exit-start`, `vehicle-exit`.
- **Not answerable from the logs:** whether Alex took `seat_front_right` and which exit gap kept her seated; both will be readable from the new lines. NCA's Judy staying out is NCA's own choice.
- **Tests.** `bridge/companion-vehicles.test.mjs` (+12 more), `bridge/companion-foreign-riders.test.mjs` (now 14). Design and lines: `docs/COMPANION_VEHICLES_DESIGN.md`, "Other mods' riders".

- **Cause.** NCA's `EnterVehicle` (`NpcManager.reds`, read only, nothing copied) mounts every follower when V gets in: its free seats are the car's passenger seats minus V's own, with no look at who already sits or is about to; favourites first, then `seat_front_right` to the best-liked rider, then the rest in vehicle-seat order; a rider with no seat is dismissed. We chose Rosalind's seat in the same moment from what looked free (NCA's followers had not started to mount, so nothing showed as occupied or reserved), so two mount commands ran for `seat_front_right`.
- **Fix (our side only).** `M.foreignRiders` in `mod/companion-vehicle-native.lua` counts, once per boarding, the followers another mod seats (the spawned-character service, V's attitude group, friendly, alive, outside every vehicle, not a drone or mech; no NCA name, tag or record). `sampleForeign` and `foreignPlan` in `mod/companion-vehicles.lua` fix the seats that plan uses (front passenger first, then the next free ones in car order, one per rider) and `available` keeps them out of our choice for 25 s; V's car only. No seat left: the existing no-free-seat path (overflow car for a driver, waiting for Alt). The pre-mount occupancy check in `board` already existed and still applies. One targeting query per boarding, nothing per frame, no new hook, no redscript, no plugin, no bridge change. Design and limits: `docs/COMPANION_VEHICLES_DESIGN.md` "Other mods' riders"; live checks: `docs/NCA_FOLLOWERS_PLAN.md` section 11.
- **Did we cause Judy not getting in?** We cannot have made NCA dismiss her: NCA dismisses a rider only when its own free-seat list is empty, and that list never counts our companions (so "seats ran out" is NCA's own count, as the live-session entry says). We could have made her mount fail or overlap, if the seat NCA assigned her was the one we took (the front passenger seat goes to NCA's best-liked rider). Which one happened cannot be told from our log: NCA logs nothing about its plan, and the car's seat count is not in the log. What is certain: before this fix our seat choice collided with NCA's first pick whenever NCA had a rider.
- **Tests.** `bridge/companion-vehicles.test.mjs` (+12), new `bridge/companion-foreign-riders.test.mjs` (9).
- **Left.** Live check (CET reload only): `docs/NCA_FOLLOWERS_PLAN.md` section 11. NCA's favourite seats are unreadable, so a favourite outside the default plan can still collide; a rider NCA seats later (after a teleport catch-up) is not planned for.
**2026-10-19 (branch `fix/report-fallback`, NOT merged or pushed): Generate report and Copy report path gave a player no feedback when the service never started; a Voxtral guardrail refusal was called a key problem.** (1) **Scripts** (`mod/`): `mod/service-status.lua` gets `reach()` (`live` / `stopped` / `never`; no evidence at all is a definite `never`, unlike `unavailable()`, which stays silent for tests and fresh installs; a trace older than this game session by more than the launcher's 3-minute head start counts as `never`). `mod/support-report.lua` `request()` now asks only a service that is up (a fresh heartbeat, or a fresh ready, starting or restarting supervisor status; it gets the 6 s wait and the banner "Creating the report…"); when `bridge-service.json` is missing, empty, unreadable or stale and nothing is fresh (before: `serviceState()` was `unknown` and the page waited 6 s for nothing), the short report is written at once. When the service never started, the report's second line is `PROBLEM: the conversation service never started ...` with the likeliest causes (Runtime missing or not loaded: `red4ext\plugins\AiNpcCyberpunkMod\`, the RED4ext log, antivirus; a Chromium browser). Copy report path without a live service writes no `clipboard-request.json` and shows the whole path (broken after folder separators, file name on its own line) in the banner and in the Copy row's help text (`support.copyUnavailableText()`, `mcm.lua`); one new string in all 15 locales, `Extract-UiCatalog.mjs --check` passes. (2) **Runtime** (`bridge/voxtral-voice.mjs`): a 403 whose own body says "guardrail" (or a plain "blocked" that does not blame the key, the account or the network and is not a web page) is a `content` refusal of that one line: no key wording, no retry, no 20 s pause, no gate tightening, no degraded state; the reply stays text-only and one line says `[Voxtral] refused this line (guardrail); shown as text`. 401 and any other 403 are unchanged. No per-reply fallback to the Convai voice: that voice is chosen when a turn starts, before any text exists, so it would need a speculative second request on every Voxtral turn. Tests: `support-report-lua`, `service-status`, `support-help-ui`, `voxtral-voice`. **Left:** the Help page's Conversation service row still says "Unknown" (not "Not running") when there is no trace at all; `reach()` could drive that label if wanted.

**2026-10-19: MO2 compatibility, step 2: the files the game and the service share exist from the start and are only modified, never created or deleted (branch `fix/mo2-step2`, from main 921b411b, NOT merged).** Design (no player log, so it has to hold with or without one): under USVFS a new file under the game folder goes to Overwrite, an existing real file opened for writing or replaced with `MoveFileExW(REPLACE_EXISTING)` stays; CET Lua can only touch its mod folder, so `runtime/` stays.
- **Built:** (1) `packaging/runtime-exchange.json` classifies every `runtime/` name the shipped Lua and bridge use; the 62 `exchange` files ship as empty placeholders in the **Scripts** zip (`scriptsPackage`), `launcher.log` ships empty in the **Runtime** zip. (2) Lua: every `.tmp` + `os.remove` + `os.rename` of an exchange file is now one in-place `io.open(path,'wb')` (one open instead of open + remove + rename, so cheaper in the game thread), and a withdrawn request (`last-input.json`), a consumed cleanup record or an emptied add-on status is an empty file, not a delete. Files in `init.lua`, `phone-chat.lua`, `auto-connect.lua`, `manager.lua` (command files), `convai-paid-tier.lua`, `voice-preview.lua`, `addons.lua`, `knowledge-state.lua`, `relationship-state.lua`, `companion-reload-cleanup.lua`, `movement-log.lua` (rotation copies into `.previous` and truncates in place). (3) Node: `addons.mjs` empties `addons-status.json` instead of removing it; every reader treats missing, empty and half-written alike (`last-input.json` poll, `world-session.mjs` with one short retry only when a ready session was held, `relationship-routing.mjs`, the knowledge service, `support-report.mjs`, the add-on state). (4) Help reports go to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AiNpcCyberpunkMod\reports` (the parent of a `data` state folder outside the mod folder; else the old `runtime/reports`); the in-game short report is one fixed in-place file `runtime/convai-report-lua.txt`; the Help page fallback now shows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AiNpcCyberpunkMod\data` and `...\reports` and the launcher path under `AiNpcCyberpunkMod` (one locale string removed from all 15 locales, none added; `localization/en.json` regenerated). (5) The legacy carry-over writes old content into an empty placeholder in place and empties, not deletes, the volatile files it purges. Tests: `packaging/runtime-exchange.test.mjs` (every `runtime/` name classified, no `os.remove`/`os.rename`/`.tmp` in shipped Lua that uses exchange files, no delete in the bridge), `bridge/exchange-files-in-place.test.mjs`, new cases in the existing Lua and bridge suites (each fails on the old code).
- **Not covered, and why:** (a) the player's own state files (`settings.json` and `.previous`, `phone-history.json`, `witness-receipts.json`, `decision-ledger.json`, `memory-chat-resets.json`, `addon-settings.json`) are not shipped (a zip extracted over an install would wipe the player's data) and keep their temp-file and backup protection, so under MO2 they are created on first write and are in Overwrite; (b) the optional native plugin's atomic write makes a `.native-tmp` file and replaces the target (unproven under usvfs; the plugin falls back to an in-place write); (c) `knowledge-fact-commits/<generation>.json` (run-time names, only the unwired fact-identity path); (d) the Audioware reply bank already ships its slots and `speech.yml`, only the transient `reply-pre-*.tmp` is new; (e) CET's own `AiNpcCyberpunkMod.log`; (f) no live check on MO2 yet: install Scripts and Runtime physically, start from MO2 with the service on, talk to a companion, quit: Overwrite should hold only CET's log and the state files; start again and talk from the first turn.
- **Decisions open:** persistent state under MO2 (settings would not survive a launch there): options are (1) leave it, (2) ship placeholders for the state files too and have the bridge keep a copy in `%LOCALAPPDATA%` that it writes back into an emptied placeholder at start (an update that wipes the placeholder then loses nothing), (3) a RED4ext-side exchange to `%LOCALAPPDATA%` (largest change).

**2026-10-18 (late): MO2 compatibility, step 1: the player's data leaves the game folder (branch `fix/mo2-state-outside-game`, NOT merged).** A player on Mod Organizer 2 (2.5.3dev2, USVFS 0.5.6.1; Scripts and Runtime installed physically, frameworks through MO2) reported that once the service had created its files, MO2 put them in Overwrite and later launches failed in CET ("Mod AiNpcCyberpunkMod failed to load!", "sol: file error: cannot open init.lua") although the physical `init.lua` was there; Skip Directories plus `enabled=0` worked around it with the service off; blacklisting `node.exe` crashed.
- **Findings (usvfs, CET and MO2 sources at master):** usvfs injects itself into every child of the game (`hook_CreateProcessInternalW`), so node.exe, Python and the hidden browser all run inside the VFS; every new file under the game folder goes to Overwrite (`RerouteW::createNew` with Overwrite as the create target), while an existing real file opened for writing, or replaced with `MoveFileExW(REPLACE_EXISTING)`, stays in place. CET checks `exists(<mod>\init.lua)` by absolute path and then runs `current_path(<mod>)` + a relative `script_file("init.lua")`; "failed to load" prints only after the exists check passed, so the relative open is what fails. Every CET mod gets a `<name>.log` in Overwrite, so an Overwrite copy of the folder alone is not the trigger; the exact usvfs path is unproven (needs the player's usvfs debug log). MO2's Cyberpunk plugin maps only the game folder and profile-local saves; `%LOCALAPPDATA%` is outside the VFS. Skip Directories only stops linking folders of that name at launch (new files still go to Overwrite and are invisible next launch).
- **Built:** `packaging/runtime/state-home.mjs`. `data/` is now `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AiNpcCyberpunkMod\data` (override `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_DATA_HOME`). The first start moves an earlier `mods/AiNpcCyberpunkMod/data` there, all or nothing (copy and SHA-256 verify into staging, then place and remove; any failure or a held lock keeps the old folder for that start). On a conflict the newer file wins and the other goes to `moved-from-game-folder/`. The old-name carry-over writes straight to the new place. `runtime/` stays (CET keeps Lua inside its mod folder). Tests: `packaging/state-home.test.mjs`, and the tests that spawn `start-service.mjs` use a temporary data home. **Runtime rebuild only**; no Scripts change.
- **Left:** done in step 2 (branch `fix/mo2-step2`, see the 2026-10-19 entry above); the player gave no usvfs log and we did not ask for one.

No need to mess with their idle settings, look-at settings or gesture ones. Actions support will not be there ... We only want to drive their face and audio when the player talks to them." Design (`docs/WORLD_CHARACTERS.md`): a named character the game placed (a roster record or name: the real Judy, Jackie, Panam, Rogue) resolves to its roster profile while Settings > Conversations > **Talk to story characters** is on (`storyConversations`, on by default; 15 locales via a Haiku helper, reviewed by tests only). `profileIdentity` passes `story`, and `characterCatalog.resolve` lets the roster record or name resolve for a `world` actor when `story` is set; it stays `world`, so a story-bound character with no roster profile never falls back to an archetype or a resident. New predicate `convaiWorldPolicy.story(npc)`; `protected(npc)` is unchanged, so the tactic target, perception, scanner name and every other system still skip them. What is driven: the reply's voice, subtitle, mouth and face (the same writer, blended emotions and blinks of speech); `beginFocus` always refuses a story character (no look-at, hold, turn, bark muting), both talk paths skip it, a group key aimed at one builds the round without it (private talk only), nothing runs for them until V talks. What is never touched: gaze, idle, gesture, workspot, movement, actions, party, attitude, equipment, scanner name, appearance. **Safety** (`mod/world-talk.lua`, new, read-only, `classify` pure): talk is refused (notice `talk-busy` "{name} is busy right now.", one probe-log line) and a playing reply is ended (`retirePrivateReply`: voice, subtitle, face reset, bridge request dropped) while the game is in charge: the character detached or dead, V in a quest dialogue choice hub, phone call or scene tier above 1, the character in a scene dialogue (`IsEntityInDialogue`), its AI commanded (`not IsOnAutonomousAI`), a fight (the character or V), injured/defeated/unconscious/stunned/ragdolled (the game's five tags), or mounted in any vehicle; a read that fails refuses. `IsEntityInScene` is never read (true in ordinary gameplay). Asked at the talk key press (fresh), the voice recording's validity poll, the moment a reply would start (`speech.start` hook) and about twice a second while it plays (`speech.update` hook, answer held 0.4 s), never per frame; `onUpdate` is untouched. **Face** (`Face.reds`): `PrepareStoryFace` at the character's spawn for a roster record (`NamedRecords`), after the screen-face step and before the crowd-graph return: the same preparation as a spawned character (gated crowd copy on a crowd graph, e.g. Jackie `man_big_sermo`; the companion graph on Judy's photo-mode graph or the paperdoll pair; anything else `unsupported-graph:` and the voice and subtitle still work); the layer is inert until the mod voices the character, nothing is rebuilt or patched. `m_storyTalk` (on in redscript) is set by `facial-playback.applyStoryTalk` at start-up and each world release; `TalkRefusal` for a roster record refuses only a dialogue (existing first check) and a commanded AI, never the quest flag or a quest-named record. The face writer judges the one story speaker (`facial-playback.storyEntity`) by the Lua checks without the broad scene flag; the idle writer stays companion-only. (her attitude to him ...), removed again`; the immediate read is worded `listed again at once, checked again below`); a weapon still drawn is asked for again once and then holstered with the unequip command itself (`N.holster`, the same `AIUnequipCommand` the equipment owner sends), never while V is in combat. **2026-10-17 (branch `voxtral-fallback`, from main cf97b9aa; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT pushed, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched): one Voxtral HTTP 403 no longer silences the voices of a group round.** Live (the user: "Voxtral stopped giving voice during a conversation but then started working again"): `runtime/bridge.stderr.log` at 09:10Z (14:40 IST) has `[Voxtral] could not speak this reply: key (HTTP 403) - did not accept the API key`, then `[VVoice] V's line was not spoken (The voxtral voice cannot be asked now (waiting out a limit))`, then `voice-routing.log` for Judy (14:40:54) and Alex (14:40:57): `used="none (written reply only)" ... fallback="Mistral cloud voice fell back (key)"`. Voxtral spoke again from 14:44:47 with the same key.
- **Cause.** `mapStatus` called every 401 and 403 a refused key; a refused key sets a 60 s cool-down in which `VoxtralVoice.ready` is false and `synthesizeHead` threw at once ("cannot be asked now") with no request and no retry (`key` was not in `RETRY_KINDS`), and the turn went to written text, not the Convai voice (only a missing key did). So ONE 403 on Jackie's reply cost her reply, V's line, Judy's and Alex's for a minute. The 403 itself: the log keeps no body, so whether it was a gateway or burst refusal cannot be proven from it; it was not a bad key (same key worked 4 min later), and it came with 3 to 4 speech requests in flight (Alex's two-part reply, V's line, the held next speaker). The 2026-10-12 measurements showed three at once all answered 200, so concurrency is a likely, unproven trigger.
- **Fix.** `VoxtralVoice.fetchPart` asks once more after 300 ms for a 403, 408, 5xx or a 429 whose Retry-After is 1 s or less (never more than a 1 s hold per turn); only a 401, or a 403 that repeats, is `key` (a 403 cools down 20 s, not 60 s). The server's words (100 chars, key scrubbed) are now in the log line. `VoiceSelection.cloudKeyless` is true while the cloud voice cannot be asked (no key, refused key, limit cool-down), so those turns are spoken by the Convai voice instead of written (order: cloud voice, quick retry, Convai voice, text; no local voice). New `bridge/request-gate.mjs` caps speech requests in flight at 4, the held next speaker (`ahead: true`, set in `convai-bridge.mjs` where the look-ahead buffers its voice) at 1 and always behind the speaker being heard, and at 2 for 30 s after a 403/429/5xx. Docs: `docs/CLOUD_VOICE_VOXTRAL.md` "Hiccups are not a bad key" and the fallback table.
- **Tests.** `voxtral-voice.test.mjs` (simulated Mistral: 5xx, 408, 403, short 429 then audio; 401 one request and key; repeated 403 key; the round of 2026-10-17; real bad key to the Convai voice and recovery; long 429; burst-guarded server with six concurrent speakers; the gate after a refusal; look-ahead never takes the speaker's slot) and `request-gate.test.mjs`.
- **To see it live (needs a bridge restart after merge):** a group round with Voxtral; `runtime/bridge.stderr.log` shows `asking again in 300 ms` lines if Mistral refuses again, and any refusal now quotes the server's text.

**2026-10-17 (branch `group-fix2`, from main cf97b9aa; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game): group chat counts every spawned character, and a spawned character's connection stays open.** Two live bugs from one test (Alex plus a spawned Jackie at about 5 m and Judy at about 1.7 m). (1) Facing Alex, F7 gave a round of two: the key press found only one spawned character. Cause: the targeting search and the native talk-target candidates both report only what the camera sees, so a spawned character outside the aim cone or behind V was invisible to every query (the earlier `group-count` fix only helped inside the cone). Fix: spawned characters seen by any query (the once-a-second auto-connect scan, group and private key presses, a talk) are remembered by entity ID (at most 12, never a handle) and resolved at the key press with `FindEntityByID`; every one within 8 m (the range group chat uses for companions) counts, wherever V faces. The log line now reads `Group candidates: ... radius=8m; counted: judy-alvarez d=1.7 via remembered, panam-palmer d=5.0 via scan; left out: <profile> d=<m> out-of-range|gone|dead|detached|disabled|...`. Limit: a character no query has ever reported cannot be found. (2) Judy's connection went away: confirmed causes: the partner role (which replaces her lane place) ended 180 s after her last turn (`no exchange` is right as designed) and she did not return to the spawned lane, which re-admits only on a scan sighting (the scan does not see her outside the camera's view); the lane also released a spawned character about 40 s after V looked away (Jackie 09:08:50, Judy 09:09:06) and had a 10-minute age limit; and the bridge (`NearbyWarm.apply`) set partners, spawned and nearby one after another with a reconcile in between, so a profile changing role was closed and opened again. Fix: a released partner that is a spawned roster character within 8 m goes straight back to the lane (cap 3, no cooldown, same write, `Auto-connect partner judy-alvarez back to the spawned lane (no exchange)`); the scan adds the remembered spawned roster characters within 8 m so the lane keeps wanting them wherever V looks; no age limit for a wanted spawned character; every speaker of a running group round counts as an exchange for a partner (before, only the addressed one did); the bridge applies the three lists as one plan change (`PartyConnections.setAmbient`), so the page stays open across a role change (plan rules unchanged: shared key 3, own paid key `min(3, limit - 1)`, free own key 0). No per-frame work. Tests: the exact case (facing our companion, two spawned characters, one outside the cone and one at 5 m, three-person round; also facing a spawned character, out of range, gone, never seen), `remember`/`recall` (bounded, IDs only), the partner returning to the lane with the connection never absent from the published lists, a full lane, a far or ordinary partner, group turns as exchange, the bridge keeping the page across partner, spawned and nearby role changes (with a control that the old sequential order drops it). `node scripts/run-tests.mjs`: 5346 pass, 0 fail, 22 skipped. Live checks and details: `docs/SPAWNED_CHARACTERS.md`, "Counting every spawned character, and keeping their connection". Needs the Lua install (CET reload) and a bridge restart; no redscript.

**2026-10-17 (branch `v-voice-engine`, from main cf97b9aa; unit-tested and measured on simulated providers, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game): V has a voice engine of its own.** The setting `vVoiceEngine` (Settings > Voices > V's voice engine) is `pocket` (default) or `voxtral`; before, V's line followed the companions' voice and Convai companions got none. Pocket uses the companions' worker when they are on Pocket, else a Pocket worker of V's own (CPU, loaded only then, never beside another Pocket worker, released with confirmed exit); Voxtral is one HTTPS request and loads nothing. Not offered: OmniVoice, the Convai voice, Inworld. V's line now starts at the top of `runInput`, before knowledge preparation and the connection set-up, so it runs beside the whole text request (about 180-200 ms earlier in every scenario). Simulated reply delay (`scripts/Measure-VVoice.mjs`), before to after: Pocket/Pocket 1634 to 1438 ms, Voxtral companions with V on Pocket 770 to 588, Voxtral/Voxtral 1623 to 1430, OmniVoice with V on Pocket 563 to 385; a Voxtral V costs the reply more than Pocket (first audio about 1.15 s). Decisions: Voxtral without a Mistral key is refused on Apply and read as unavailable, no silent fallback to Pocket; a failed cloud V line is not retried; Mature content keeps V off the cloud; both engines English only; a Voxtral V line is skipped while the Mistral scheduler is spacing or paused. Tests: `v-voice`, `v-helper-voice`, `resource-lifecycle`, `manager`. Docs: `docs/V_VOICE.md`, `docs/RESOURCE_LIFECYCLE.md`, `docs/MANAGER_UI.md`, README. Live check in the list above.

**2026-10-17 (branch `group-count`, from main 9415fdc4; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game): group chat counts spawned characters whoever V faces.** Live bug: facing one of our companions with two characters another mod spawned nearby said "needs two characters". Cause: the first build added spawned characters from one scan that kept roster profiles only, so a scan miss or a generic profile (a ganger, a custom NPC) left only the companion; facing a spawned character worked because that character is always counted and the companion made two. Fix: candidates are the scan plus the spawned characters among the key press's own native talk-target candidates, generic profiles count (two on one profile are two people; the audience lists the profile once), and the key press logs what it found and why it dropped some. Live check: the third step of the phase 2 list in `docs/SPAWNED_CHARACTERS.md`.

**2026-10-17 (branch `spawned-face`, from `integrate-1017` 1983cbba; unit-tested and the redscript compile check passed, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, no game input): a spawned character's lips did not move; the cause is a rebuild nobody prepared, fixed in `Face.reds` (`docs/SPAWNED_CHARACTERS.md`, "Lips did not move").**
- **Live result (`integrate-1017` build).** A spawned Jackie and Judy talked with their own voice, but `probe.log` read `face=false/prepared:man_big_sermo` and `face=false/prepared:player_woman_photomode_sermo` (our own Alex: `face=true`). The graph names were right (Jackie is the big-man crowd graph, Judy's own graph is her photo-mode graph); the status word was stale.
- **Cause.** The spawner calls `ScheduleAppearanceChange` right after it creates a character. The rebuild replaces `face_rig` with the vanilla graph, and its `Entity/Extract` names no entity (ID 0, no entity part), so the managed lookup in `OnCompanionExtract` skipped it. Phase 1's claim that rebuilds were caught was never true. `ConvaiFaceReady` (live graph path against the prepared one) then correctly said false. No archive of the spawner touches Judy's or Panam's face graph or rig (the Judy facial fix is one new `.app` that needs an ArchiveXL `.xl` patch, not installed; the body revamps are meshes and textures).
- **Fix (`r6/scripts/CyberpunkConvai/Face.reds`).** `NoteRebuild` notes the `face_rig` clones of an entity-less, entity-part-less extraction (weak refs, at most six, only after a spawned character was seen) with a key for the entity template; `OnReassemble` (registered once, `NPCPuppet`, first line exits) prepares the notes of a spawned entity's own template with `PrepareSpawnedFace`, before the new components initialize, and updates the puppet's status and graph path. `ConvaiFaceStatus` now reports `stale:<graph> noted= claimed= reassembled= unmatched=` for a prepared face that runs another graph, and `ConvaiFaceRequest` returns it (a `Face request:` log line). Our own companions and game characters are not matched; no per-frame work.
- **Tests.** `bridge/facial-graphs.test.mjs`: three pinned contracts updated (Reassemble is now registered, once), one new contract for the note-and-claim pair (guard order, bounded and weak, the claim by template, status and request, no write outside `PrepareSpawnedFace`). `scripts/Compile-Redscript.ps1` compiles. Full suite (`node scripts/run-tests.mjs`, PowerShell): 5330 tests, 5308 pass, 0 fail, 22 skipped.
- **Live check owed (Scripts install and a game restart).** Spawn Jackie and Judy with the spawner, wait for its appearance change, talk by text: `face=true/prepared:...` and moving lips; then change an outfit and talk again; Alex still `face=true`. A `face=false/stale:...` line says where it was lost. Unverified assumptions: the rebuild's extraction precedes its `Reassemble`, and the clones noted are the ones the entity receives.

**2026-10-17 (branch `group-latency`, from `integrate-1017` 1983cbba; unit- and harness-tested, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched, no game input, no bridge restart): group rounds on the player's own Convai key ran every speaker change serially; look-ahead now runs on a confirmed paid plan.**
- **Live evidence (the user: "both answer in turn, latency seems a bit much though for character after first one").** `runtime/bridge-latency.json` of the game, 12:27 IST round on the player's key (`GamerPlanV2-Monthly`, Voxtral voice, three speakers: Jackie, Alex, Judy): the later speakers read `preparation.mode: "none"` and waited 8.3 s (Jackie to Alex) and 9.0 s (Alex to Judy) between the previous speaker's last audio and their own first audio (`requestToResultMs` 13.5 and 16.1 s; `receivedAt` 94 and 103 ms after the previous `continuousPlaybackCompleteAt`). Where it went, per later speaker: connection 3.0-4.3 s (`pageReused: false`, a page more per speaker), reply 2.4-2.6 s, pool wait 0.4 s, voice first audio 1.1 s, publication 0.4 s, all after the previous speaker had finished. No prefetch was discarded and nothing queued behind speaker 1's audio: nothing had been started.
- **Cause.** `pollLookahead` (`bridge/convai-bridge.mjs`) returns while `singleSession()` is true, which is true for any player's own key (`keys.singleSession`), free or paid (`docs/CONVAI_PAID_TIER.md` said so on purpose, to save interactions). It had nothing to do with spawned characters or the voice provider. The first speaker is quick because V's own voice line plays beside its request.
- **Fix.** `lookaheadAllowed` (`bridge/group-lookahead.mjs`): look-ahead runs on the shared key and on a player's key whose confirmed plan holds two or more connections (`connectionLimit()`, 6); a free, unknown or unread plan and Mistral or the local AI stay serial. On a confirmed paid plan the first speaker's request also opens the other speakers' pages (`warmRoundAhead`: `RealtimeHost.warm` of the exact route, never awaited, sends nothing, writes no memory), because the 3.5 s connection otherwise starts only when the previous speaker's text is complete and leaves about 2.2 s. Solo turns, private chats, prefetch and the pre-opened party, phone and ambient connections are unchanged. Spawned-character speakers need nothing special: the game side publishes the same prediction for them (new Lua test) and the bridge sees a roster profile and an entity id (new module test).
- **Numbers** (real bridge, simulated game, provider delays shaped like the live round, three speakers, `node scripts/Measure-GroupGap.mjs --fixture --key player-paid --live-timings`): player key on a paid plan before 7.5 s and 7.6 s; look-ahead only 2.4 and 2.5 s; with the pages opened at the first request 0.31 and 0.38 s; free plan unchanged 7.2 and 7.4 s. Details in `docs/GROUP_VOICE.md`.
- **Tests:** `bridge/group-lookahead.test.mjs` (the plan gate, a spawned speaker's prediction held and claimed), `bridge/group-chat.test.mjs` (a spawned speaker before and after our companion gets the same prediction and the prepared turn), `bridge/group-lookahead-bridge.test.mjs` (three: paid against free with live-shaped delays, a speaker alone unchanged, a round of two). The fixture gained a player key with a plan limit (`fixtures/fake-paid-tier.mjs`, no plan is read from Convai), a connection cost per speaker and `warm` events.
- **To install:** `bridge/` only (a bridge restart); nothing in `mod/`.
- **Live check owed:** with the own key on the paid plan, a group round of two or three; the later speaker should follow the first within about a second (`runtime/bridge-latency.json`: `preparation.mode: "lookahead"` on the later turns, `connectionWarm`, and the gap from the earlier turn's `continuousPlaybackCompleteAt` to the later turn's `continuousPlaybackFirstObservedAt`). A round on the shared key and a solo turn must read as before. Not changed and still costing a solo turn on a player's key 3-5 s: the connection is not pre-opened for a private chat (`deferWarm`); that is a separate decision (interactions and memory-user slots on a player's key).

- **Baseline (the user's live test of the build before this branch).** The scanner shows no level or threat for a companion (normal for followers), so level scaling is verified by the log read-back only. Alex draws a weapon and fights in an ordinary fight. An attack order with a gang member tagged in the scanner (out of combat, within 100 m) was answered "Tag an enemy in your scanner or aim at someone first." `probe.log`, five times: `Tactic candidates: 1 NPCs within 100m, 0 tagged, via IsTaggedinFocusMode; Alena Xenakis 1m tag=no`, then `Tactic target: none; skipped aimed-companion=1`. The search returned only the companion; the tagged NPC never became a candidate.
- **Part A, target enumeration (`mod/companion-marking.lua`).** Cause: the only candidate source was the targeting search (`GetTargetParts`, filter NPC, tested set Complete), which in that test reported nothing but the companion beside V. Why it missed the gang member is not known (distance, line of sight or the tested set; the log will say). Fix: the game keeps every tagged object in the blackboard `TaggedObjectsList.taggedObjectsList` (`FocusModeTaggingSystem`, public script dump `focusModeTagging.script`). One on-demand read per request (never per frame) now adds every NPC on it within 100 m as a candidate, tagged, with the same exclusions; a read of `IsTaggedinFocusMode` (the game's spelling, it asks the ScanningController the tagging system writes to) that says no beats a stale list entry, an unreadable read is settled by the list. The search still supplies untagged NPCs for the aimed and nearest steps. A look-at that lands on a companion is skipped and the crosshair line is followed to the NPC beside her. The candidates line gains `tag list K (M missed by the search, F beyond 100m)` or `tag list unreadable (...)`, so the next log shows whether the list or the search was at fault.
- **Item 4 (`mod/companion-tactics.lua`).** Hostile attitudes alone can leave a follower watching, because her Follower reaction preset ignores hostile stimuli (`reactionComponent.script`). For the tactic only: an aggressive preset (`Ganger_Aggressive`, else `Mercenary_Aggressive`, `Corpo_Aggressive`, else the first aggressive non-civilian, non-police preset by name), the old one kept in the receipt; then, after the attitudes and the threat, `TriggerCombat(target)` on the companion's reaction component (a civilian-record copy uses `AIActionHelper.TryStartCombatWithTarget`). Every end of the tactic puts the preset back (read back, logged), also when the target is already dead, unless the game has chosen another preset since; a gone companion is not touched; a start that fails halfway rolls back preset and attitudes. Every step is optional and logged as `Companion tactic: reaction: ...`. One tactic at a time and the marking rules are unchanged.
- **Item 5 (`mod/companion-records.lua` `prepare`, called once from `attachFollower`).** Only a copy with our spawn tag: the game's `NPCManager.ScaleToPlayer` through `npc.m_NPCManager` (fallback: the same three stat calls), level read before and after; the attitude group and the attitude towards V read back once, a difference re-read once 1 s later from the existing tick. No per-frame work. Switch: `runtime/companion-scaling-off`. Game characters and other mods' spawns are never touched. Docs: `docs/COMPANION_COMBAT.md` "Combat readiness at attach", `docs/COMPANION_TACTICS.md` "Fight".

- **Before:** `mod/companion-locomotion.lua` observed `AIMoveToCommandHandler.UpdateCommand`, which the game runs every AI tick for every walking NPC. Even with no companion out, each call paid the CET call into Lua before the early return; with a party each call also did `GetOwner` and the ownership loop.

Safety: at install a reflection check (or the Observe call) decides; if the script half is missing or older, or `runtime/locomotion-engine-hook.txt` exists (kill switch for the first release), it registers the old engine observer, and a failed mark registers it at once, so the stale-facing clear is never lost and start never breaks. The `M.active` teardown gate is unchanged. `perf-probe.lua` rows carry `locomotionHook`. No new per-frame or main-thread work; vanilla NPCs pay one type test and one Bool read in script.
- **Measured (unit level, headless: `node scripts/Measure-LocomotionHook.mjs`, production Lua in fengari against a model of the hook, 600 to 1500 ticks):** calls into Lua per 1500 ticks with 0 companions and 50 or 200 ordinary walkers, before then after: 75,000 then 0 and 300,000 then 0 (also 0 `GetOwner` calls). With 3 companions and 200 walkers: 304,503 then 4,503 calls (only the companions' own 3 x 1,501), same for `GetOwner`. Lua time per call for an ordinary walker in fengari, before: roughly 12 to 15 microseconds with no companion out and 20 to 90 with three (the runs are noisy), after: not entered. Per tick with 3 companions and 200 walkers: 4 to 16 ms before, under 1 ms after (all of it the companions' own 3 calls and the model's wrapper). These are fengari-relative; the real CET trampoline per call is not in them and is the larger saving in the game. Stale facing cleared for 3 of 3 companions before and after.
- **Tests:** `bridge/companion-locomotion-filter.test.mjs` (7: mode choice, every fallback, mark and its failure fallback, ordinary NPCs never enter Lua, marked walk reported and facing cleared, teardown gate, the redscript wrapper text and the packaging lists); the existing `companion-behavior` locomotion tests unchanged.

**2026-10-15 (branch `convai-signin`, from main 86c01521; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT tried against the live login page): Sign in with Convai.** Research (read-only): the user's chess app (`Conv-AI/Classic-Chess`) read Convai's `.convai.com` login cookies (`CONVAI_AUTH`, `CONVAI_API_KEY`) and decrypted them with `POST https://login.convai.com/api/decrypt`, which only works on a convai.com subdomain. Dharmik's app (`Conv-AI/ConvaiConnectDemo`, Unity) uses a separate Firebase project and its own Desktop OAuth client, and gets no Convai key yet. Convai's login page already has a desktop hand-back for its Unreal plugin (`Conv-AI/Convai-UnrealEngine-Auth`): `https://login.convai.com/?ue=true&port=N` sends the browser to `http://localhost:N/control?api_key=<encrypted>&user_info=<encrypted>`. The mod now uses that: `bridge/convai-signin.mjs` (a one-shot loopback listener for at most five minutes, the decrypt call, the key checked as Paste checks it and saved through the Paste path), a `sign-in` action in `PaidTierControl` that answers `signing-in` at once, and a **Sign in with Convai** row on the paid tier page with one message per outcome (8 new strings in all 15 locales). No outside change needed. Remaining risks (encrypted values in the loopback URL, no `state`, an open decrypt route) and the Firebase `/user/login` fallback are in `docs/CONVAI_PAID_TIER.md`, "Sign in with Convai".

**2026-10-15 (branch `convai-paid-tier`, after merging main a479d8fc; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT installed): paid keys hold several conversations at once.** The user's answers: on a confirmed paid Gamer plan, a player's key may hold up to six Convai connections, so several companions talk and generate together. Warm-ups, look-ahead and prefetch stay off for every player key. Free, unknown or unread plans keep one connection. How: `exclusive.limit()` in `bridge/realtime-host.mjs` closes only the idle connections beyond the cap, oldest first. `PaidTierControl.connectionLimit()` is memory-only. The plan is read in the background only while the player's key is in use: once per key, again after 6 h, with a retry 10 min after a failure, and an answer is trusted for at most 12 h. A failed read means one connection. Sign-in stays paste-your-key, with a `signIn` seam for a future Convai login endpoint. The backend is not deployed (built-in plans). The README's one spot mentions several companions at once.
