Yesterday's call was a method of `SceneSystemInterface` and there is none: a probe compiled with `scc.exe` against the 2.31 cache (isolated copy, game untouched) says `method 'IsEntityInInteriorArea' not found on 'SceneSystemInterface'`, while `IsEntityInScene(EntityID)` resolves. The real one is a **global** script function, `import function IsEntityInInteriorArea( entity : weak< Entity > ) : Bool;` (`tools/redmod/scripts/core/entity/gameEntity.script` line 5), used by the game's own `weaponTransitions.script` and `reactionComponent.script`. Now `Game.IsEntityInInteriorArea(player)`, guarded, on demand only, logged as `indoors=true|false(IsEntityInInteriorArea)` or `indoors=unknown`. (2) The picture was 52 s old (`bridge.stderr.log`: `turn …: 1 image(s), frame 52 s old`, taken outside): the helper is released during a conversation and the buffer preferred frames from before it, so a long conversation sent stale frames, or none. **Fix:** a picture older than 15 s is never sent (was 2 minutes); when a turn starts (composer opens, talk key) and no frame is under 6 s old, one frame is taken then (about 0.35 to 0.5 s with the helper start, hidden behind typing or talking; the helper is released again by the next poll), a staged frame older than 15 s at the send is replaced, a turn with nothing staged waits at most 450 ms for a capture, and a turn without a picture logs why. **Quality (the user: "vision wasn't great"):** 1024 px at JPEG quality 88 (was 768 at 80; Convai `max_resolution` 1024), measured 112 ms and 16 ms helper CPU against 109 ms and 16 ms before; a single game picture darker than 70 of 255 is lifted with a gamma curve in the hidden browser; the HUD (about 10 to 12 %) is left in. **Precedence:** the context note that goes with a picture now says the text's indoors or outdoors is fact, else judge it from the image and never from the district's name; the turn-context wording and the pinned prompt are unchanged. **Dev option:** `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_VISION_DEBUG_LAST=1` or `"visionDebugLastSent": true` keeps the last picture sent in `runtime/vision-last-sent.jpg` (+ `.json`). Tests: `bridge/companion-vision.test.mjs` (8 new or rewritten), `bridge/convai-vision.test.mjs` (3 new), `bridge/turn-context.test.mjs` (the Lua adapter rewritten for the global call, one new), plus `scripts/lua-upvalues.test.mjs`. Install: `mod/turn-context.lua` (done, CET reload); after the merge `npm run build:voice` and a bridge restart (child `bridge/convai-bridge.mjs` only). Live checks: "Indoors and fresh pictures" above.
**2026-10-15 (branch `mic-fix-4`, from main 5fe2f0e8; unit-tested; Lua hot-installable, bridge needs a child restart): the talk key did not stop a recording, and loops passed the filter.** Live record: a Bluetooth hands-free headset ("Default - Headset (realme Buds Air7)", 16 kHz) recorded 29.95 s and 27.14 s (about 7 s of sound, 2 s voiced) and decoded to "Destiny, destiny, destiny, ..." and "... tooth tooth on tooth tooth"; the user: "when I press F8 it doesn't stop recording". Cause 1 (key): F8 was a CET `registerHotkey`, which runs only when the key comes back UP (`docs/COMPANION_HOTKEY_INPUT.md`). Holding it did nothing until it was let go, a stop press was seen only on release, and presses during the 2 s a Bluetooth microphone takes to open are ignored by design ('connecting'), so both recordings ran to the Lua 30 s cap (the game log shows `finish` only 30 s after the start). Fix: F8 and the group key are now `registerInput` (press and release): a press on a recording finishes it on the press itself; a tap (up within 300 ms) toggles; a hold that began the recording finishes on release (still a toggle if the device is still opening). Every edge, the recording state and the command source (`press`, `release`, `cap`, `*-delayed`, cancel reason) are logged; the bridge logs each command with its source and ms into the recording, closes the device the moment the stop arrives (`MicrophoneSession.stopCapture`: before the context refresh and the 700 ms minimum) and logs 'capture closed N ms after the stop command'. Echo: nothing the mod speaks can start during a recording (the key stops all voices and clears the subtitle; add-on remarks and battle/loot reactions wait; pinned by a test); the game's own sound and the headset's own sidetone are outside the mod. Silent device: a recording whose loudest moment is under -55 dBFS (now measured on the whole recording, not only on decoded pieces) ends as `MIC_SILENT`, state `silent` with the device name, and the game shows 'The microphone {name} sends no sound. Check your Windows input device.' (`mic-silent`, 15 locales, catalog regenerated). Loops: `judge` now drops one word three times in a row among others, a 2-3 word chunk three times in a row, one content word making a third or more of six words or more, and 3 s or more of sound with under 35% voiced (speech measured 51% and up, the headset recording about 30%); the two live texts are test cases. Tests: `bridge/knowledge-integration.test.mjs` (tap, hold, hold while opening, key repeat, logged edges), `microphone-adapter.test.mjs`, `local-stt-capture.test.mjs`, `local-stt-worker.check.py`. Open item: the user tests F8 (tap to start, tap to stop; hold to talk) and the headset.
**2026-10-15 (branch `holocall-face`, from main 64f913fd; unit-tested, reds compiled, NOT merged; `mod/holocall.lua` hot-installed and seen working by window capture; the reds and `phone-chat-style.lua` changes are installed and need the game restart to be seen): the holocall copy's face moves, she faces the lens, and the Chat tab's underline is the game's red (`docs/HOLOCALL.md`, "Face" and "Gaze").** (1) The user: on a holocall she looked a little left of the camera and her face never moved. The speech path was already right (the reply's face goes to the copy; the last live holocall turn wrote 387 frames to it, jaw peak 0.58, not blocked). The cause is distance: the game stops animating a face far from V's own camera. Measured with a dev probe (`runtime/holo-face.lua`, one `ConvaiFaceApply` jaw 0.9 / blink 1, the studio forced to chosen floors): jaw and blink show at 2.5, 5, 7.8 and 11.2 m from V and not at 15.8, 19.2 and 42.5 m (the earlier picture was 42 m below V). Forcing `clientForcedLod`, `clientForcedVisibility` and `useLongRangeVisibility` on `face_rig` at run time changed nothing. Fix: the studio search tries near floors first (within 11 m of V: straight over or under V and a 5 m ring, floors 10 m up to 10 m down), then the old columns; the probe line gains `away=<m>`. From the Corpo Plaza apartment a normal call put her 5.1 m away (the floor above): jaw, blink and a replayed talking timeline through the real writer (face-test `face-play`) all moved. Also, as an experiment for far studios, `Face.reds` asks the holocall copy's animated components for full detail before they attach. (2) Gaze: the game's holocall scene (`judy_holocall.scene`, `scnLookAtEvent` "Eyes & Head") turns eyes, head (0.1) and chest (2), nothing suppressed; the copy now gets that with head 0.3, and faces the lens in captures. Before, only the eyes were asked to turn, and a frozen far face could not turn them. (3) The user: the Chat tab's underline was white when not selected. In `phone-chat-style.lua` the tint copy walked the icon's children, but the icon is an image with no children, so the error stopped the function before the underline got its colour. Now the icon and label bind the game tabs' own `MenuLabel.MainColor`/`MainOpacity` (red in Default, the active blue in Selected, the same style the game's tab panel uses), the underline binds `MainColors.PanelRed` as the game's tab lines do, and the tab's state is set as the game's `UpdateLabelsStates` does (in `PhoneChatTabs.reds` and the styler). Tests: holocall (near search, look parts), phone-ui-localization (bindings and state, a leaf icon), phone, ui-catalog suites pass; `Compile-Redscript.ps1` compiles. Live checks after the restart: the tab colours, and whether the copy's face also moves at a far studio (the `Face.reds` experiment); still owed: her lips following a real reply's voice.

Cause, from `runtime/movement-trace.ndjson` and `probe.log` of the 2026-10-14 19:54-20:05Z session (Alex, V still at -53.7,-1131.3 for the whole trace): the mod did not walk her. Her follow brain stayed `settled`/`attend` `hold`, the hold command was `Interrupted (4)` (the gesture workspot owned the body), and no `Companion teleport` line was written. Her body slid inside the idle workspot `convai_idle_generic_hips` (vanilla `female__stand_around__02`): at 19:56:57Z, 25 s after it began, speed 1.2 m/s, gap 1.3 m to 1.8 m (0.7 m); at 20:00:36Z, 30 s after the next one began, speed up to 2.0 m/s, gap 1.8 m to 3.7 m (1.9 m). The other idles she played in those 11 minutes (`idle_alex`, `idle_jackie_hips`, four plays of 65-75 s) never moved her. The cycle is the idle flavour scheduler: an idle of 45-90 s, a gap of 20-45 s, another idle, so slides come at regular intervals. Older evidence: 7 `Gestures drift` lines in `probe.log` from 2026-10-14 05:42Z on, 6 of them `convai_idle_generic_hips` (one 1.95 m at 17:20:42Z), the other `panam_hips` 0.17 m; `convai_idle_generic_hips` entered the generic pool in 6dfdfda3 and 8f1802a0 (2026-10-11), and bdc1d5a2's TODO of 2026-10-13 (gesture-slide) already said a `drift` line with V still would mean a per-component fix. Not the cause: no wander or ambient-spot feature exists, the follow command is not re-issued on a timer (the only periodic thing is the `hold` resubmit about every 100 s at the same spot, which moves nothing), seating was not in use. Fix (`mod/companion-gestures.lua`, no new per-frame work, uses the existing gesture tick): (1) `policy.travellingIdles = {generic_hips = true}`: that idle is never picked (the other woman idles jackie_hips and panam_hips stay; Claire, whose own idle it was, gets those); (2) `policy.driftExit = 0.45`: an idle flavour that carries the body more than 45 cm from where it began, V still, is left at once (`Gestures drift-exit`, `finished` reason `drifted`) and the idle key is learned for the session (`self.travelling`), so no companion takes it again; ordinary settling of 15-25 cm stays. V walking away still ends every idle with `movement` and the follow code is untouched, so following works as before. Tests in `bridge/companion-gestures.test.mjs`: never `generic_hips` for an uncatalogued woman or for Claire over 14 rounds each; three companions idling, one drifts 90 cm and only she leaves while the other two keep their idles, and the drifted idle is never played again; V walking off ends all three with `movement`, nothing learned. **2026-10-15 (branch `companion-vision`, from main 404ad14c, merged with main 00e7b682 (e0c03b68) and 79e03690; unit-tested, capture measured against the running game with no input; NOT merged into main, NOT installed, no live Convai turn): Companions can see the surroundings.**
- **Research** (`docs/COMPANION_VISION.md`, with links):
  - The realtime Web SDK 1.7.0 we use takes pictures two ways: dynamic vision context (a LiveKit video track sampled by the server into a buffer and attached to the next model turn, with acknowledgements) and `uploadFile` (a byte stream; server behaviour undocumented). Publishing before the text is the documented streaming mode.
  - Vision is account-gated and needs a non-realtime Gemini or GPT model. Our Gemma 4 31B Fast is listed among the realtime models, so `vision_not_enabled` is possible; only a live call can tell.
  - Auth-token mode is unaffected. No per-image price or rate limit is published.
  - Mistral (Ministral 3 takes images on the same endpoint) is postponed by the user. Local AI needs Gemma's mmproj: a download and about 1 GB more VRAM (not built).
- **Design history:** the first build sent a talk-time picture only with lines asking about something visible; then a picture on every turn. The user then pointed out a talk-time picture mostly shows the companion's face, and asked for the surroundings with V and the companion small or absent.
- **Built (final):**
  - Setting "Companions can see" in the Conversation provider section, **on by default**, Convai only.
  - An out-of-process Windows Graphics Capture helper (`native/vision/`, C++/WinRT) captures only the game window: a 768 px JPEG in memory, nothing on disk, `minimised` reported.
  - A rolling buffer (`bridge/companion-vision.mjs`): one picture every 3 s, the last 4 in memory, only while the setting is on, Convai answers, someone V can talk to is near, and no conversation is running (plus 12 s after one). A turn sends the newest frame taken at least 2.5 s before the conversation started, so it shows the place V was looking at, not the companion; nothing older than 2 minutes.
  - Latency: the chosen frame is published to Convai when the composer opens (each speaker's page in a group, retried while a page connects) and right after the talk-key press, so Convai's estimated 0.4 to 0.7 s acceptance overlaps typing or talking. At send the page sees the same picture already staged and waits for nothing. A turn not staged ahead waits at most 350 ms (`visionWaitMs`), beside the context update. An unclaimed picture is withdrawn when the composer closes or after 60 s.
  - The unload rule (`docs/RESOURCE_LIFECYCLE.md`): the helper process exists only while it is capturing; it is stopped when the setting is off, under Mistral or Local AI, with nobody near, or during a conversation.
  - One sentence in the context says the image shows the surroundings from a few seconds before, may show the HUD, V's vehicle or the companion, and not to guess without one. Any failure sends the line without a picture.
  - `companionVision.attachToNextTurn(images, {characterId, ttlMs})` is the entry point for the YouTube-on-TV feature.
- **Measured:**
  - Capture every 3 s: round trip 107 ms median (p95 133), helper CPU 15.6 ms median. Helper start about 0.2 s, cold start plus first capture 338 ms, memory 35 to 51 MiB.
  - Game FPS A/B every 3 s (two runs, 12 and 16 blocks of 20 s): 57.41 against 57.41, and 55.49 against 55.47 (means). Slow frames were not more frequent in windows that held a capture (0.40 per window) than in "with" windows that held none (0.54). The isolated long frames (217 and 227 ms) fell in windows without a capture.
  - Added latency (estimates): talk key about 0; typed with the composer open first about 0; otherwise at most 350 ms.
- **Four views around V:** not built. Script has no render-texture readback; each extra camera is a full scene render every frame, plus streaming hitches; camera or photo-mode moves are visible. The buffer gives a view of the place at no measured cost.
- **The TV as the source** (user, via the coordinator): while a YouTube video plays on V's TV, about one 640 px frame a second of our own TV window (DevTools screenshot, no game capture; the game helper is released) is fed as a live canvas track to the party companions' open pages, which reconnect between conversations with five frames a turn (`TV_VISION_INPUT_CONFIG`). Turns publish nothing and wait for nothing; the context says these are the last seconds of the video. Nothing is grabbed or published without a playing video, with the setting off, under Mistral or Local AI, or with nobody near. API: `youtubeTv.visionSource()` and `companionVision.setScreenSource()`, wired in `convai-bridge.mjs`. Measured against the running game (not seated, game in the background, about 60 fps): no TV 58.97 FPS median, video without frames 59.91, video with 1 frame a second 59.94 (frames over 25 ms per window 0.15 / 0.36 / 0); a grab takes 13.9 ms median in the bridge and returns 14 KB. 2 fps not measured (the game was restarted by someone else mid-run, no crash report).
- **Two bugs fixed in the merged YouTube TV window helper** (`bridge/youtube-tv-window.ps1`, found running it for real): Windows PowerShell 5.1's `[Console]::In.ReadLineAsync()` runs synchronously, so the helper blocked waiting for a second command before handling `attach` while the bridge waited for `attached`, and the TV never opened; and Edge titles the window "<title> - Profile 1 - Microsoft Edge", which the exact title match never found. Now a `StreamReader` over the raw stdin and a prefix match (the title has a random nonce). Regression test in `youtube-tv.test.mjs` runs the real helper.
- **mcm.lua diff:** one `setting('companionVision', …)` row right after the Conversation provider selector, and `companionVision` in the Apply boolean key list.
- **Tests:** `bridge/companion-vision.test.mjs` (20), `bridge/convai-vision.test.mjs` (17), 3 realtime-client cases, 1 youtube-tv case; manager row lists updated; 2 strings in 15 languages; `localization/en.json` regenerated.
- **Live check:** under Open items B2. It needs the user's approval for about 5 to 10 Convai turns.

**2026-10-14 (branch `v-voice-omni-drop`, from main 8f0b4992; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT heard or seen in the game, game not touched, no live turn; bridge restart only): V's typed line is now audible with an OmniVoice companion.** Live log: `engine=omni result=dropped reason=reply-voice-started` at 0.88 s and 1.06 s, so V was never heard. Cause: V was rendered whole on OmniVoice's single GPU worker (about 1.3 to 1.9 s to anything audible), the companion's text reply is ready at about 0.9 to 1.1 s and its own OmniVoice request stopped the unheard V; that worker cannot cancel a started render, so the reply's render queued behind V's anyway (late reply for nothing, plus a hidden GPU render and a CUDA graph capture per typed line). Fix (`docs/V_VOICE.md` "OmniVoice companions"): beside OmniVoice, V is spoken by a Pocket worker on the CPU (new `bridge/v-helper-voice.mjs`, wired in `bridge/voice-selection.mjs` `tickVHelper` and `bridge/v-voice.mjs` `helper`): loaded once in the background after OmniVoice is ready, only while OmniVoice is committed and the V setting is on, released before any other Pocket worker starts (one work-folder lock), never beside a cloud voice, the Pocket voice or the Convai voice. Estimated (not measured live): V audible at about 0.25 s, reply start 0 to 0.3 s later than with V off for an ordinary line and 0.4 to 0.9 s sooner than the old path; the options (a) play V on Omni first with a cap (reply at about 4 to 4.5 s, GPU cost) and (c) start earlier (already done, 3 to 7 ms) were rejected. Costs: one extra Python process, the 418 MiB Pocket student plus runtime, CPU only, 0 VRAM, about 45 s background load; no V on a non-English turn beside Omni (Pocket is English only); a failed helper means silent V until the setting or voice changes. New tests: `bridge/v-helper-voice.test.mjs` (9), nine Omni cases in `bridge/v-voice.test.mjs`. Packaging lists (`packaging/runtime-layout.mjs`, `packaging/release-plan.json`) gained the new file. Live check: "V's voice with an OmniVoice companion" in Live checks owed.

**2026-10-14 (branch `holocall-native-look`, from main 3e1e7b2f; unit-tested, redscript compiles against the real game cache; NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched): holocalls follow the game's own video/voice rule, and the live picture is rebuilt the way the game films a caller.** Research (extracted quest files in `research/cyberpunk/cache/game/raw/`, the 2.x script dump, and a third-party holo studio write-up with in-game measurements, github.com/blackpotoftea/cyberpunk_docs `holo_studio/`): the game's video holocall is `holocall_camera.ent` (`RenderToTextureCamera`) filming the caller's real body in an out-of-bounds lit studio into `holocall_camera_render_texture.dtex`, which the call window's holocall image shows; `StartHolocall` only switches the window. The mod cannot use that path (quest facts, scenes, a global lock). **2026-10-14 (branch `delamain-voice-mute`, from main 3e1e7b2f; unit-tested in fengari and node, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched, no live Convai turns, nothing pushed; main part needs a CET reload of `mod/addons.lua` and `mod/game-dialogue.lua`, the add-on part is in `cyberpunk-convai-delamain`): the Delamain cab's own welcome and goodbye are switched off and the add-on's own play in their place.** Why the cab voice could not be muted: it is not script code. The 12 Delamain lines of `delamain_taxi.scene` are played by the scene system and the audio director (Wwise VO switches set natively), nothing in redscript starts or stops them, so there was no call to hook and no event name; the add-on declared `audio = {}` and could only hide the subtitle. The runtime `line.id.hash` is a small counter, not the string id, so the lines are recognised by the speaker name (the exact ids are recorded in the add-on's `line-ids.lua`). Two mechanisms. (1) **Welcome:** the game has its own skip switch, the quest fact `delamain_skip_dialog` (scene node 730: set, the scene skips the greeting and goes straight to the Ready state and the destination map, then clears the fact itself). The add-on sets it from `ObserveBefore DelamainTaxiComponent.OnVehicleStartedMountingEvent` when V starts to climb in at state 1 or 2 (one fact write, before the scene reaches node 730 about 1 to 3 s later), puts it back only if V gets out first, the cab is ready with it still set, or the player turns the option off mid-boarding, and writes no other fact; the map, the fare and the drive are the game's. Its own welcome is asked for as soon as V sits down (the ride record now starts at the mount and survives the Ready write), so it is generated while the game opens the map, plays about when the map appears, waits like every remark for the scene and game lines, and is dropped for the ride-start greeting if V picks a destination first. (2) **Goodbye, arrival and "your wish is my command":** no switch exists, so the main mod stops the voice with `AudioSystem.Stop(event, speaker entity)` for `vo_3d`, `vo_2d`, `vo_3d_important` (candidates: the tag-less core VO events) and filters the subtitle, over a window that now starts when V climbs in and ends with the ride (states 1 to 7, V in or entering the cab). New in the main mod: `N.stopAudio` returns a function that re-sends the same stops (it holds the entity id value and the event names, never the entity), `ruleLine` hands it to `M.mutedLine` as `info.repeatStop`, and `M.tick` repeats it at 0.3, 0.8 and 1.6 s (at most 6 lines tracked, dropped on `M.reset`; only for a rule that has voice events), because a scene voice can start just after its subtitle. The goodbye stop is **not heard-tested** (`audioVerified` stays false: a remark still waits for a line that keeps playing, so the worst case is the old order, the game's goodbye then ours). The persona, trigger guidance and the `gameVoiceReplaced` fact now make Delamain greet and say goodbye himself while the game's lines are off (and not repeat them when the option is off). "Replace the game's own lines" and "Mark our lines (AI)" work as before; with the option off nothing is written and the game's lines play. Tests: add-on 56 (55 against this branch's main, the one failure is the unrelated `remarkCap = false` assertion another session added, which needs main-side support not on this branch; 56 against the main checkout), main `addons-lua` 29, `game-dialogue` 21, `addons` and add-on neighbours green. Live check (also item 10 of the live list in `docs/ADDON_API.md`): ride a cab with the option on; the cab's greeting must be silent with no subtitle, the map must open a few seconds after sitting down, and the add-on's welcome must play about then; at arrival read probe.log for `muted game line: Delamain ... audio=stop-sent(vo_3d,vo_2d,vo_3d_important)` and listen whether the game's goodbye really stops; if it still plays, the next candidates are other Wwise events (see the add-on's `docs/DELAMAIN_RESEARCH.md` 2.4) and `volume_dialogue`; check that `delamain_skip_dialog` is 0 again after the map opens. Install `mod/addons.lua`, `mod/game-dialogue.lua` and the add-on folder, CET reload.

**2026-10-14 (branch `skippy-hologram`, from main 15e2d625; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT heard or seen in the game, game not touched): Skippy remarks that showed a subtitle but could not be heard; his voice from the gun; why the game's hologram text cannot carry our remarks.** Cause of the silent remarks, from the 2026-10-14 logs: the bridge cut remarks the game had already accepted. The reaction lease (`runtime/reaction-lease.json`) said `playing` only on the add-on tick after the game accepted the reply, and its deadline was floored to whole seconds (`os.time()`), so a short remark could look expired the moment it began. Example from probe.log: companion-kill played and was released in the same second, and the bridge logged `Continuous speech owner changed`. Separately, one refused or half-written lease read (Windows sharing, an atomic replace in flight) made `reactionCurrent` return false, and `tick()` aborted a playing turn. During play the lease is rewritten every second (fight-start was cut about 1 s in). Fixes: `canDeliver` writes `playbackStartedAt` at once (`mod/addons.lua`); the deadline adds a second for the rounding; `reactionCurrent` retries EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES/ENOENT and half-written JSON three times, 15 ms apart, and keeps a playing turn through up to 1 s of unreadable lease (`bridge/convai-bridge.mjs`). New `reactionLeaseProblem` (`bridge/battle-context.mjs`) names the reason. New log details: ` voice-stopped=<speech state> (<error>)` on `Remark released` when the voice ended early, and `(lease: <reason>)` on the bridge's `did not reach the player`. Voice position: new speaker option `voiceFrom` (`docs/ADDON_API.md`); Skippy passes his active weapon, so the browser voice takes its pan and distance from the gun (asked once per reply, dropped back to V if the gun is not within 3 m of the camera; the native Omni phrases still play on V). Hologram: the game's text beside the gun is a fixed onscreen string per voice line id (`vo_onscreens`, 19 entries, all mq007), drawn by something no script feeds. `Invisible` lines are rejected by both script subtitle controllers, so our text cannot be routed there and the subtitle fallback stays (detail and sources: `docs/addons/SKIPPY_RESEARCH.md` 1.4.1). Tests: `battle-lease` (retries, the bounded grace, refusal reasons), `addons-lua` (playing at once, the deadline, voice-stopped, voiceFrom, the init seam), `continuous-speech` (gun position, fallback, ordinary replies untouched), `loot-context` (adapter). Live check: Live checks list, "Skippy remarks heard and his voice from the gun".

**2026-10-14 (branch `clip-search-43`; CPU/GPU jobs finished and stopped, game not touched; bridge restart needed; NOT heard by anyone): the remaining 43 voices re-searched with a loudness band; their references re-picked (OmniVoice) and gain-matched (all).** The pool is level-matched at about -23.6 LUFS (median of 42 of the 43 voices between -23.4 and -25.1; `jesse` is hot at about -17), so the band bonus (`scripts/clip-search/loudband.py`, full bonus -22 to -16 LUFS, penalties below -22 and above -16, true peak and squashed-sound terms, clipped or noisy clips never candidates) could only move the OmniVoice sets by a few tenths of a dB: 13 of 43 short and 30 of 43 long sets got different clips. `search.py --loud` (with `--seed-scores`, `--tag`, `--voices remaining43`) ran the 43 voices in 115 min on the local GPU; the Pocket run was stopped on the user's decision after one voice (all its processes killed, none left). The user then chose: OmniVoice = the new picks, Pocket = current picks, every set gain-matched towards -20 LUFS with one linear gain, no limiter. First pass used a -3 dBFS peak ceiling and lowered 11 to 17 quiet sets per kind (their peaks already exceeded it); the user corrected that (louder, never quieter), so the rule is now ceiling -1 dBTP (EBU R128), gain = max(0, min(gain to -20, gain to the ceiling)) below -20 LUFS, sets between -20 and -16 left alone, sets hotter than -16 turned down to -20 (only `jesse`). Result, mean level before to after: Omni short -23.2 to -20.6, Omni long -23.3 to -20.9, Pocket -23.2 to -21.1; sets still under -20 LUFS (held by the -1 dBTP ceiling): 18 short, 24 long, 28 Pocket (of 43 each); no quiet set got quieter. `scripts/clip-search/loud43/apply_loud43.py` wrote 172 WAVs into `runtime/voice-references/picked/autobest/{omni-short,omni-long,omni,pocket}/` and updated only the 43 voices' entries in `pocket-voices.autobest.json`, `local-voices.autobest-short.json`, `-long.json`, `local-voices.autobest.json` and `runtime/autobest-sets.json` (every other entry byte for byte; backup of the originals in `runtime/backups/clip-search-43-20261014/`, kept through both passes); `loud43/validate_configs.mjs` and the bridge's Python validator pass for all four configs (hashes match). Next: restart the bridge, the user listens (`docs/CLIP_SEARCH_43_2026-10-14.md`, "Listen first"), then the bucket upload. A true-peak limiter would bring the remaining sets to -20 (not done, ruled out).

**2026-10-14 (branch `addon-game-lines`, from main 87438a3a; unit-tested; NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched; install all committed `mod/` files, the bridge (restart) and both add-ons, then a CET reload): Skippy remarks that never played, the game's own Skippy and cab lines, and a marker for our lines.** Live report: "new message detected", "provocation" and beeps, no way to tell the game's lines from ours, the AI remarks seemingly not playing. probe.log showed almost every Skippy remark cancelled, not-delivered within the same second, or stale. Causes found: (1) **cancelled** = the add-on's own `vanillaSpoke`: any `Invisible` subtitle line while Skippy was held (the game's bark scene, name key `LocKey#46444`) cancelled whatever was waiting; (2) **not-delivered in the same second** = the bridge's local-AI pace: `LOCAL_REMARK_GAP_S` (20 s) is counted from the start of the previous remark on the local route, including the cancelled and stale ones, and a refusal (`addon-pace`) lost the moment; priority 5 (near death, fight end) was refused too, and so was the Delamain arrival; (3) **stale** = a cold or contended local model with no patience (Skippy's remarks had none, ttl 3 s). Fixes: the bridge no longer refuses priority 5, tells the game the spacing (`gap`) so it waits instead of asking and being refused, and gives the pace back for a remark that never reached the player (`remarkRefunded`, in a try/finally in `runAddonTurn`); every Skippy event now has patience by priority (5: 12 s, 4: 8 s, 3: 6 s, 2: 4 s) with `relevant` = still holding Skippy, and his speaker plays through ordinary scenes; his own subtitle hooks and the cancel are gone. **Replacing the game's lines** (new API `handle:replaceGameLines`, `docs/ADDON_API.md`): per add-on option **Replace the game's own lines** (default on) and **Mark our lines in the subtitles** (default on, adds ` (AI)` after the add-on speaker's name). The subtitle is hidden by one `Override` of `SubtitlesGameController.ShouldDisplayLine` installed on the first rule (fallback: `HideDialogLine` right after); the voice by `AudioSystem.Stop('vo_3d_important', speaker)` for Skippy; for the cab there is no known voice event, so **only its subtitles are hidden and its voice still plays** (the earlier "our welcome right when the game's would have come" is not done: it needs a verified voice stop). Skippy's claim: speaker named Skippy or `LocKey#46444`, or an `Invisible` line with no readable speaker name while he is held; Delamain's: speaker named Delamain while V sits in the cab; no other line is touched; the scene, map and payment are never skipped. Tests: bridge pace (priority bypass, token refund), game-dialogue filter/fallback/stop, addons-lua rules/settings/muted-line/silenced-scene, subtitle marker, Skippy and Delamain rules. Pre-existing failures in this worktree, not from this change: `facial-timeline` and `companion-actions` pinned SDK (node_modules absent here) and two packaging allowlist tests (`bridge/v-voice.mjs` missing from the list, from the V-voice work). **Next live test, probe.log lines:** `Game dialogue: subtitle filter installed`, `[Addons] muted game line: Skippy <id> (subtitle=filtered audio=stop-sent(vo_3d_important) ...)` (does the voice really stop? if not, the stop does not work for scene dialogue), `[Addons] Remark: ...`, `Remark played: ... event=... after Ns`, `Remark released: ... reason=... refused=<code> spoken=<bool>`, `Remark dropped: ... reason=...`, and `muted game line: Delamain <id> ...` on the cab ride; bridge.stderr.log: `remark ... did not reach the player; it does not count towards the local pace`.
**2026-10-14 (branch `v-voice-clips`, from main 87438a3a; measured, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT heard by anyone, game not touched, GPU not used): V's reference clips re-picked by the project's automatic picker.** User report on the Pocket voice: V's line sounds "a bit off, a little low quality" (gender and timing right). Inspection of the first clips: no gross defect (no clipping, peaks -5 to -8 dBFS, clean floor, no radio or phone filter, no music or SFX bleed, 24 kHz, loudness within 1 dB), but they were chosen by ASR match and loudness only; nothing measured speaker likeness, and it was poor: ECAPA to six held-out real V lines 0.537 (male) and 0.429 (female). The extractor also never looked at the scene index (12 percent of V's quest lines are inner-dialog, cyberspace or phone expressions; the first picks happened to be plain Spoken). Fix: V's lines went through the same flow as the companions: `build_v_pool.py` (1200 lines per gender in the picker's pool format with its effect exclusions plus dull, noisy, hot and the combat/expression flags from the scene index) then `search.py` (Pocket student v2 on the CPU, one low-priority worker, cap 18 s) then `compare_v.py`. Result on the same held-out lines: male 0.673 (search pick, 2 clips, 10.65 s) and 0.677 (3 clips, 13.6 s, shipped: calm opening, same score within one SE, higher on the four typed test sentences), female 0.521 (2 clips, 11.55 s; the search pick, shipped). Honest note: PLS is slightly higher for the old male clips (121.5 vs 115.7); the old clips were clean, they lacked likeness. ASR on the renders 0.98 to 1.00. `assets/v-voice/v-voice.json` is updated and committed; the new `v-male.wav` / `v-female.wav` / `v-voice-build.json` are in this worktree's `assets/v-voice/` (git-ignored, copy them into the main checkout with the merge and into the installed `voices/v-voice/`); the manifest and clips must be installed together (the bridge checks the hash). `GAP` in `scripts/clip-search/v-voice/vcommon.py` is now 0.4 s (the project's reference recipe, what the search scored). New scripts: `build_v_pool.py`, `run_search.py`, `compare_v.py`. Listening files (old and new references, rendered sentences, real V lines, README table): `C:\Users\akshi\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\v-voice-candidates\`. Open: the user listens (`ref_old.wav` vs the winner, `test*_old.wav` vs `test*_long.wav` male / `test*_auto.wav` female); if it still sounds low quality the cause is Pocket's rendering, not the reference (artifact measures of the renders are in the normal range of real V lines). `docs/V_VOICE.md`.

**2026-10-14 (branch `delamain-arrival`, from main 0f3abd5e; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched; needs a CET reload of the Delamain add-on): a false "destination reached" in the Delamain cab.** Live ride (probe.log, 20:35 UTC on 13 Oct by the log clock): V sat in the cab with Alex aboard, set a destination on the map, and 3 s after `ride-start` the game's own state went to Arrived (5) with the cab standing still; the game's Delamain also said "destination reached", so the add-on only mirrored the game. Evidence it is the vanilla taxi and not the mod: every main-mod hook on the taxi or AutoDrive is an Observe with read-only bodies (`mod/init.lua` `OnAutodriveToggled` after, `OnStopAutoDriveOnDestinationReachedRequest` before); the only `Override`s are phone, MCM and subtitle UI classes; the only setters near the cab are the companion mount and unmount commands (`mod/companion-vehicle-native.lua`, V's companions, not the cab) and `DisableAutoDriveRequest` in `companion-chauffeur-native.lua` `M.disable`, which refuses a Delamain journey and is only for old reload receipts; the add-on itself never writes a fact; the probe log shows no companion exit or chauffeur line near the event. What we cannot see: why the game said Arrived (the destination distance was not logged, so a point already near the cab, a stale value or a quirk of picking the point right after the greeting are all possible). Fix in `addons/delamain/init.lua`: an Arrived signal counts only after the cab moved at least 25 m (or half the start distance for a destination closer than 50 m) since `ride-start`, measured from V's position read once at the Started event (no polling); a re-plan (Started again) resets the origin; boarding (Ready) again clears the old plan, start time and arrival flag; an ignored arrival keeps the talk phase at "riding" and logs one line `[Addons] delamain-cab: arrival ignored (moved N m since ride-start, needs M m)`. Tests: five new cases in `addons/delamain/delamain.test.mjs` (the live sequence, a small creep, re-planning, boarding again, a zero-distance destination); the whole file, 40 tests, passes. Live check: take a cab, pick a point, and watch probe.log; if the game says "destination reached" before the cab drives, there must be an `arrival ignored` line and no `event=arrival` remark; a normal ride must still end with the arrival remark. If it fires on a ride that did drive, raise nothing: read the "moved" number in the line.

**2026-10-14 (branch `teardown-safety`, from main 7d1379a8; unit-tested; NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched): session-teardown review after two crashes during a save load (`Cyberpunk2077.exe+0x53F9D4` on 14 Oct, one second after "Session references released: player detached"; `+0xE6ABAD` on 12 Oct). Neither stack contains the native plugin (it only registers RTTI natives, holds no game object between calls and installs no hook). No single culprit is proven; four paths that made engine calls on objects being destroyed, and several strong handles that pinned them past the unload, were closed.** (1) `companion-locomotion.lua`: the `AIMoveToCommandHandler.UpdateCommand` observer (every walking NPC, every frame) stayed switched on after `companions.abandon` because only `companions.update` refreshed `convaiLocomotion.active`, and update is skipped until the next session is up; with a party it therefore called `GetOwner(context)` and `npc:GetEntityID()` on AI contexts the engine was destroying. It is now false from the start and set false in `companions.abandon` (fast travel too; the next update turns it on again). Both crash sessions had mod companions. (2) Add-on hooks (`addons/delamain`, `addons/skippy`) ran with no session check: the cab hooks read the quest system and `component:GetEntity()` during the unload, and Skippy's weapon-swap and crosshair hooks read the player and weapon (and could set `holding` true again after `sessionEnded`). New add-on API call `handle:live()` (true from the first tick of a session until the main mod releases it; documented in `docs/ADDON_API.md`); both add-ons return at once when it is false. Delamain counts the ignored callbacks by name and logs them at the next session start ("cab callbacks ignored while the previous session was released"), which shows which callbacks the engine sends during a teardown. A cab found at the start of a session is still picked up by `sessionStarted`. (3) `seated-look.lua`: the Workspot exit hooks called `CancelDelay` on the engine's delay system (and the pending id was never cleared) while the player's state machine left Workspot during a load; with the session released they now only forget (`live` = not `worldSuspended`, passed from `init.lua`); entering is not gated so a save loaded while V sits is still widened. (4) Handles held across the unload (a CET handle is a strong reference, and `onUpdate`, which would have cleared them, does not run until the next session): the face writer's cached actor rows (`companions.expressionActors` cache plus the `convaiExpressionFrame` context) held every ready copy's and nearby candidate's NPC; the gesture and seating controllers held V (`self.player`); the MCM page held old settings-screen widgets (`statusOriginal`, `contentHold`) and would have called into them on the next update. All dropped in `abandonSession`/the modules' abandon; `abandonSession` then runs one `collectgarbage` (not on fast travel, never per frame; unproven in game, a one-off hitch at a load) so the engine objects are released while the world still owns them, not by a Lua finalizer in the middle of the unload or the next session's start. Not changed: adoption records keep a hidden world NPC across a fast travel on purpose (needed to show it again); `mod/face-test.lua` (developer tool) has no abandon. Tests: `bridge/companion-behavior.test.mjs`, `bridge/companion-duplicates.test.mjs`, `bridge/companion-expression-playback.test.mjs`, `bridge/seated-look.test.mjs`, `addons/delamain/delamain.test.mjs`, `addons/skippy/skippy.test.mjs`. Reviewed and found sound: the whole `abandonSession` chain (pure Lua, file writes only, no native call), `companions`/`vehicles`/`actuator`/`equipment`/`reload-cleanup` abandon, speech/subtitles/continuous speech, `ConvaiTurnStep` delay callbacks (weak refs, generation checked), Codeware callbacks registered by UI controllers (unregistered in `OnUninitialize`), `ConvaiKnowledgeState` (unregisters in `OnDetach`). Still suspicious, unchanged: the Codeware `Entity/Extract` callback in `Face.reds` (untargeted, runs `GetDynamicEntitySystem().IsTagged` for every entity the engine builds, including during session start and end; a `dynamic.IsReady()` guard was NOT added because the redscript API could not be verified without the compiler); `Session/BeforeEnd` (already registered in `KnowledgeState.reds`) fires before the player detaches, while the Lua mod only learns of a teardown at `PlayerPuppet.OnDetach`, so callbacks arriving before that are not gated; the un-gated UI hooks (`phone-input.lua`, `phone-layout.lua`, `phone-chat-style.lua`, `subtitles.lua` `ChatterLineLogicController.SetLineData`).

**2026-10-14 (branch `crouch-relaxed`, from main 5279552f; unit-tested; NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched): companions did not crouch outside combat because the stance alone shows nothing in the Relaxed state; the crouch now raises the high-level state first, with a head-height read-back.** Live (probe.log 19:29Z): V crouched outside combat, `Companion stance: crouch hls=Relaxed (evelyn-parker)`, no retry line, and Evelyn stayed standing; `stand hls=Relaxed` 23 s later. The stance request was accepted (no error, no `crouch again`, so the stance blackboard read Crouch), yet no pose. Cause, from the decompiled 2.31 scripts (`cyberpunk/NPC/components/npcStateComponent.swift`, `NPCPuppet.swift`; fetched read-only from the public dump already cited in `docs/addons/SKIPPY_RESEARCH.md`): `NPCPuppet.ChangeStanceState` only queues an `NPCStateChangeSignal`; `NPCStatesComponent.UpdateStanceState` then sets the `stanceState` anim feature, the Stance blackboard and the `inCrouch` wrapper weight. The locomotion wrappers that carry the walking poses are keyed by the HIGH-LEVEL state (`GetAnimWrapperNameBasedOnHighLevelState`: Alerted `alertedLocomotion`, Combat `combatLocomotion`, Stealth `stealthLocomotion`, Relaxed none). So in Relaxed nothing consumes the crouch (this is the likely cause; it is read from code, not yet seen in game, and the new head reading will decide it). Vanilla followers crouch only when their own AI is in Stealth. Ways the game itself reaches Stealth, all read in the dump: `NPCPuppet.ChangeHighLevelState(npc, Stealth)` from `AIFollowerTakedownCommandHandler` and from the move command handlers when `alwaysUseStealth` is set (AIMoveTo/AIMoveOnSpline/AIMoveRotateTo, NOT AIFollowTargetCommand, which has no stealth or crouch flag: fields are target, desiredDistance, tolerance, stopWhenDestinationReached, movementType, lookAtTarget, matchSpeed, teleport), plus the `StealthState` AI task. `AIFollowerRole.OnHighLevelStateEnter(Stealth)` barks only with a hostile threat; the Stealth case of `OnHighLevelStateEnter` in the state component does nothing (no senses preset change, no registration). Alerted by contrast calls `TryRegisterToPrevention` and `RefreshCachedReactionPresetData`, and the installed `ApproachVehicleDecorator` refuses boarding while Alerted, so it is the fallback, not the first choice. Companions never enter Alerted on their own (`AlertedCondition` returns false for player companions). Fix (`mod/companion-stance.lua`): crouch = `NPCPuppet.ChangeHighLevelState(npc, Stealth)` first (only from Relaxed; a state the game chose is never changed), the stance call 0.15 s later (two state-change signals in one frame may overwrite each other), then the Head slot height above her feet is read once after the stance call (same `GetSlotTransform('Head')` read `init.lua` already uses) and compared with her standing height read before the crouch: down 0.2 m or more = confirmed; not down within 2 s = the next method (Alerted), then none (Relaxed restored, the old stance-only behaviour). Stand: stance Stand first, then Relaxed 0.15 s later, only while the state still reads the level we raised (never over Combat, Fear, Unconscious); both read back, re-issued every 0.6 s up to three times, head compared with the standing height; `stand not kept by the game` if still wrong. If the AI resets the raised state to Relaxed while crouched, it is raised again up to three times, then `keeps resetting`. A stand because of a blocker (vehicle, lift, tactic, ...) restores Relaxed too, and V crouching again before the restore keeps ownership of the raise. No per-frame work: one 10 Hz tick, one blackboard observer, bounded timers (0.15 s gap, 0.6 s read-back, 0.5 s re-check while crouched, head read until confirmed only). Known side effects while she is crouched in Stealth: gestures stay off (they already do), and the holster handoff waits for Relaxed (`NPC is not relaxed autonomous AI`). **Log lines for the next live test (install `mod/companion-stance.lua`, CET reload; all start `Companion stance:`):** V crouches: `crouch issued via stealth (hls Relaxed -> Stealth, then stance Crouch) stance=Crouch hls=Stealth`, then within about 1.5 s either `crouch confirmed via stealth: head down 0.4x m stance=Crouch hls=Stealth` (works), or `crouch NOT visible via stealth: head down only 0.0x m ...; trying alerted` followed by `crouch confirmed via alerted: ...` (Alerted works, Stealth does not; make `methods = {'alerted'}` the default), or `crouch NOT visible via alerted ...; no method left, hls back to Relaxed` (neither works: the pose needs something else, e.g. a direct `stealthLocomotion` wrapper weight, and the head numbers tell how far off), or `crouch confirmed via stealth by the blackboards only (no head reading)` (the Head slot read failed: then judge by eye). Other lines: `crouch: hls fell back to Relaxed, raised again (stealth)`, `crouch: the game keeps resetting hls to Relaxed after stealth`, `crouch not kept by the game`. V stands: `stand issued via stance, then hls Stealth -> Relaxed stance=Stand hls=Stealth`, then `stand confirmed stance=Stand hls=Relaxed, head back (0.0x m below standing)`; bad cases `stand: blackboards read Stand but the head is still down ...`, `stand again`, `hls Relaxed again`, `stand not kept by the game`. If the stand line shows `hls=Stealth` after confirmation, gestures will say `not relaxed`: report it. Also watch that she draws no weapon and nobody nearby reacts. Tests: `bridge/companion-stance.test.mjs` (35 tests; 14 new: order and gap of the two calls, stand restore, Alerted escalation, no-method fallback, game-chosen states untouched, combat takeover, AI reset retries, ignored restore, crouch-again ownership, blocker, no-head-reading, stance-only adapter, bounded reads, adapter wiring).

**2026-10-14 (branch `delamain-timing`, from main 5279552f; unit-tested in fengari and node, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not launched, no live Convai turns; needs a bridge restart plus a CET reload): the Delamain cab's welcome, ride and goodbye lines no longer collide with the game's own cab lines, no longer get cut off, and no longer get lost.** Live report from the user's second cab ride: the first message never played (too close to the intro), his replies were cut off abruptly, the welcome and ending did not play (they probably coincide with the game's own message), and the driving looked messy (he hit cops and a fight started). Causes: (1) cut-off replies: a bridge bug, not timing. `continuousSpeech.onGenerated` in `bridge/convai-bridge.mjs` threw "Conversation receipt owner changed" for every add-on turn, because an add-on speaker has no knowledge receipt; the reply was cut when the first chunk landed (seen in bridge.stderr.log). Fixed: an add-on turn with no receipt skips the knowledge calls and only has to be the current turn (a turn that lost ownership is still rejected). (2) welcome and ending lost: the game's `delamain_taxi.scene` plays its greeting and farewell as quest-scene subtitle lines, and the host only knew scene flags from the 0.5 s observer sample; a flight that met a scene was released and never asked for again (the old retry only covered queue drops). (3) first message lost right after the intro: the same path, plus a pending request with no reply held the queue (36 s seen). Fixes in `mod/addons.lua`: a remark can have `patience` (seconds) and a `relevant()` check; while a game scene, a scene tier or a game subtitle line is up it is held, not dropped (its ttl does not run), and sent after the scene clears plus 1.2 s of quiet if still relevant, with a fresh clock; a patient remark taken back in flight (a scene hit before it was heard) is asked for again, twice at most; a request that gets no reply within ttl plus 2 s is withdrawn ('stale') so it cannot block later remarks, and a patient one is asked again; no game line playing means no wait at all. New `M.gameLine(seconds, kind, measured)` is fed by `mod/game-dialogue.lua` `noteLine` (Regular, OwnerlessRegular, Holocall, SceneComment and Radio lines, once each, with their own duration or an estimate of 2.5 words/s, clamped to 1.5 to 10 s; the mod's own replies, crowd chatter and TV never count), through `onGameLine` in `mod/init.lua`, only while an add-on is live (no cost otherwise, no per-frame work; the host's 0.1 s tick already runs only while an add-on is live). A speaker can set `playThrough`: a line already playing finishes over an ordinary scene (dialogue, choices) instead of being cut; a call, Johnny (replacer), a tier 4+ cinematic or the player's own turn still stops it. Why play through rather than hold the game's subtitle off ours: the cab's greeting and farewell are a quest scene we cannot delay or reorder, so the workable options are to wait for it before we start (done) and not to be cut by it once we have started (done). Delamain add-on (`addons/delamain/init.lua`): a `WAIT` table gives each event its patience and the ride states it stays relevant in (boarded 30 s / READY, ride-start 20 s / STARTED, district-passed 12 s / STARTED, arrival 25 s / ARRIVED or FINISHED, ride-interrupted 20 s / CANCELLED); the arrival and goodbye stay relevant briefly after the ride ends while V is still in the cab; the old RETRY machinery is removed; a destination chosen while the greeting still waits turns into one ride-start line that greets (the greeting is cancelled; one line, not two). Docs: `docs/ADDON_API.md` (Patience section, `playThrough`, `requeued`, new reasons), `addons/delamain/EVENTS.md`. Tests: `bridge/addons-lua.test.mjs` (patience, relevant and expiry, requeue twice at most, stale withdrawal, game lines, playThrough), `addons/delamain/delamain.test.mjs` (welcome taken back and said again, game line holds the greeting, plays through, arrival after the farewell, no arrival to an empty cab, destination chosen during a held greeting), `bridge/game-dialogue.test.mjs` (noteLine), `bridge/voice-routing.test.mjs` (add-on turn without receipt); the harness `bridge/addon-lua-harness.mjs` now names the failing test line. Full suite: only environment failures in this worktree (no `node_modules` here: facial-timeline, the companion-actions SDK adapter test, the runtime-bootstrap playwright test) plus the known timing-flaky voxtral spacing test, which passes alone. The unknown only the game can settle: which scene signal the cab ride raises (dialogue, tier, or only a subtitle line); the logs name it. **Driving verdict: nothing in the mod or the add-on writes to the cab's driving.** The Delamain add-on is voice only (it reads ride state from the `delamain_taxi_state` fact and the observer; it never sets vehicle or driver AI, speed or route). The main mod's chauffeur modules (`companion-chauffeur-native.lua`, `companion-chauffeur.lua`) explicitly refuse the Delamain cab (`delamainCab`) and treat a foreign AutoDrive journey as someone else's; the companion vehicle code only seats companions (taxi seat order is back-left, front-right, back-right, front-left last, so the driver seat is used only with four or more companions); seated gaze writes look-at only; the work done while the cab moves is read-only sampling. The cop collision is most likely the game's own autodrive (the vanilla Delamain does hit traffic and police); it cannot be ruled out from code alone, so a live A/B is the answer. Cleanest live A/B: the same short ride, same start and destination, twice: once with the mod disabled in CET (or add-on and companions off, nobody in the party), once as in the report; also read probe.log for `Native core: vehicles=native|lua`, `journey-start`, `seat-reserved`, `mount-requested`, `taxi-arrived`, and check that no companion took `seat_front_left`. **Log lines to look for in the next ride:** `[Addons] Remark held: ... reason=scene|scene-tier|game-line signals=... patience=Ns` (what held it, and the signal the cab scene raises), `[Addons] Remark: ... waited=N.Ns` (it went after the wait), `Remark released: ... reason=scene signals=... (taken back; it is asked for again)`, `Remark plays through a game scene: ... signals=...`, `Remark dropped: ... reason=expired|irrelevant`, `Game line: <kind> for about X s (its own duration|estimated); patient remarks wait for it`; in bridge.stderr.log there must be no `Bridge request failed: Conversation receipt owner changed` for Delamain turns.
**2026-10-14 (branch `v-voice`, from main 5279552f; unit-tested, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT heard in the game, game not touched; needs a bridge restart plus a CET reload for the Lua and locale files): new setting "V's voice for typed lines" (Voices, off by default) speaks what the player types in V's own voice, cloned from clips cut from the game's V lines.** User request: a setting so that, only for typed input, V's voice is generated so it sounds like V said the line. Design and detail: `docs/V_VOICE.md`. (1) *Setting*: `vVoice` in `mod/manager.lua` (default Off, snapshot field, bool validation, `M.vVoice()`), a row after Follow-up questions in `mod/mcm.lua` (also in the Speech line of the Characters sidebar), the bridge reads it from `runtime/settings.json` in `pollSettings`. (2) *Voices*: the setting uses the voice the player already chose. Pocket and OmniVoice clone V locally; Mistral (Voxtral) and Inworld clone in the cloud and load no local voice model. The Convai cloud voice cannot clone: turning the setting on beside it is refused with a short message, choosing the Convai voice while it is on keeps the voice and turns V's voice off with one notice, and a saved pairing loads as off. (3) *Clips*: one reference per gender cut from the game's own V lines (male 11.4 s from 3 lines, female 14.5 s from 4 lines; `scripts/clip-search/v-voice/`, Oodle plus vgmstream on this machine, CPU only, Whisper small.en matches every subtitle 0.94 to 1.00). **Nobody has listened to them and they are not approved.** `assets/v-voice/v-voice.json` (hashes, transcripts, sources) is committed; the `.wav` files and `v-voice-build.json` are git-ignored like the add-on clips and `packaging/build-release.mjs` packs them from the local copy into `voices/v-voice/` (a build without them works and logs it). They are merged into the voice configurations at bridge start as `v-male` and `v-female` (`AddonHost.voiceConfigPaths` `extra`, lazy, so nothing is loaded for them; `withoutVariants` keeps them out of every profile list). (4) *Latency*: the typed text goes to the model as before and V's line starts after that request is under way (`runInput`); it plays on a second hidden renderer page (`RealtimeHost.playVoiceLine`) with its own control (no game utterance, so no face, lip sync or subtitle). The companion's audio waits only while V is audible: the existing continuous-speech `hold` buffers it silently (a reply published whole waits in `publishResult`). A V line that is not audible when the reply is ready is dropped; one still waiting for its first audio when the companion's own `ttsSent` mark comes is stopped on a local voice. Timings: V's own `TurnClock` (`voiceStart`, `ttsSent`, `firstPcm`, `audible`, `ended` or `dropped` with a reason), one `[VVoice]` log line and a `vVoice` record in `bridge-latency.json`; the companion's clock gets `vAudible`, `vEnded` or `vDropped`. (5) *Gender and volume*: V's gender is the turn context's `gender` (`GetResolvedGenderName`); the game's Master x Dialogue volume is read once per typed turn while the setting is on (`dialogueVolume` in `mod/turn-context.lua`, cached 5 s with the rest). Nothing runs per frame. (6) *Tests*: `bridge/v-voice.test.mjs` (clips, line text, WAV to packets, gating, the real local renderer host with an offline player, the real continuous speech held by V), plus additions to `manager`, `turn-context` and `addons` tests; `bridge/turn-clock.mjs` gained `on()`. `packaging/runtime-layout.mjs` lists the new module. 15 locales plus `localization/en.json` got the four new strings (translated by a Haiku helper: a native-speaker pass can follow). `packaging/runtime-bootstrap.test.mjs` cannot finish in the worktree (no `node_modules/playwright`); its allowlist comparison passes up to that point.

**2026-10-13 (branch `picker-no-auto`, from main; unit-tested with the fake llama-server, NOT merged, NOT installed, NOT seen in the game; needs a bridge restart plus a CET reload for the Lua and locale files): the Local AI model row has no Auto entry; it lists the installed models from the smallest file to the largest.** User request: "Remove Auto from the model picker of Local AI; just sort them from small to high." (1) The row (`mod/mcm.lua`, `manager.localModelChoices()`) lists only the installed models, sorted by file size, equal sizes by name (the bridge publishes them sorted, `describeLocalModels`; `manager.lua` sorts again). The labels are unchanged: sizes in the help, "(custom)", "too large for this graphics card" (a too-large model stays listed and shows as unusable; choosing it falls back). With no model installed the row shows one placeholder, "No model installed". (2) The default (no saved choice, or a legacy `localModel: auto`) is the largest model that fits the free graphics memory, the rule Auto used. The bridge publishes it as `localModelDefault` (and `localModelMatureDefault`, below) in `mistral-state.json`, computed by the pure `defaultModelIds` from the free memory the last start saw before it loaded (`LocalLlmServer.lastFreeMiB`), else the card's total (the existing single `nvidia-smi` call, now also when more than one model is installed; no new polling). The row shows that model as SELECTED; the next Apply stores its concrete id (`manager.applySettings`, silent, no notice). Until then a saved `auto` still loads the same default, with no fallback notice. (3) Mature preselect: turning Mature content on stages the largest uncensored model that fits (`localModelMatureDefault`) with the line "Uncensored model", or nothing for the model when none is installed or none fits; turning it off restores the previous model (a legacy record with `set = auto` still restores). (4) Fallback: a chosen model that is missing, too large for the free memory or did not start is replaced by the largest model that fits (the largest uncensored one first with Mature on); the notice now names it: "The Local AI model you chose is missing, does not fit in the free graphics memory or did not start, so {model} was used instead." (the `model-fallback` event carries `model`, the reply carries `keyNoticeModel`); once per change, as before. (5) The custom manifest `auto` flag is obsolete: accepted whatever its value, ignored, documented as obsolete. Custom models take part in the default and the fallback by size and fit; `uncensored: true` counts for the Mature preselect and fallback (`autoEligible` removed). (6) Docs: `docs/LOCAL_AI.md` ("Choosing the model", "Add your own model", developer notes), `docs/NOTIFICATIONS.md`, `docs/MANAGER_UI.md`, the player and Mature pack readmes. New or changed UI strings are in all 15 `mod/locales/*.lua` (machine-translated by a Haiku helper, one German string spot-checked); `localization/en.json` regenerated. Tests: `local-model-choice`, `custom-model-choice`, `custom-models`, `local-llm-server`, `mistral-key` and `manager` updated and extended (sorting, default selection, legacy `auto` migration, Mature preselect with an uncensored model and with none, fallback naming the model, custom `auto` ignored). Not live-tested: the row's look in the MCM (a long list of models; the placeholder), whether the default shown matches what loads on the real card, and the Mature toggle staging the uncensored model. Uncertain: the default shown comes from the free memory seen at the last start (or the card's total before any start), not from a fresh reading, so it can differ from a later load if other programs change the free memory; a model already shown selected is saved as a concrete id on the first Apply, so later memory changes then use the fallback notice instead of silently choosing another model.

(2) `emotion-tags` 1457, `expressive-emotions` 1488 and `natural-speech` 2798 counted `transformReply: cleanReply` in `convai-bridge.mjs` as 3 (conversation, phone, Mistral); the add-on speakers' text host (`addonTextHost`) legitimately passes every reply through the same cleaner, so the count is 4 and the messages say so. (3) The Invite voice preparation block in `bridge/voice-routing.test.mjs` (13 tests, 16-22 and 28-33): `tick` and `pollMicrophone` now read `addonHost.isSpeaker` and `addonVoice.voice`, which the test sandbox did not define (ReferenceError); the sandbox now has stand-ins that claim nothing. In a worktree with no `node_modules` of its own, `companion-actions` (pinned SDK), `facial-timeline` and `packaging/runtime-bootstrap` (allowlist) read `node_modules/...` straight from the project root and fail; that is the worktree, not the code.
**2026-10-13 (branch `custom-local-models`, from main; unit-tested with the fake llama-server, NOT installed, NOT live; needs a bridge restart plus a CET reload for the Lua and locale files; not merged): players can add their own GGUF chat models by hand to the Local AI model row.** A player drops a `.gguf` into a `custom/` folder of the Local AI folder and lists it in `manifest.custom.json` (`{version: 1, models: [{file, name?, uncensored?, auto?, family?, contextSize?, chatTemplate?}]}`; also read from the dev Local AI folder when only that has it). `bridge/custom-models.mjs` validates each entry strictly (relative path inside the folder, `.gguf`, name 1 to 60 characters, booleans, `contextSize` 2048 to 262144, `chatTemplate` name; at most 16) and logs each bad entry once as `[custom models] ...`, never throwing. Requirement checks run at detection time on the settings poll (at most every 5 s, never per frame; stats every look, the first 2 MiB of a file read only when its size or time changed): GGUF magic and version 2 or 3, `general.architecture`, an embedding model rejected from its architecture or a non-zero `<arch>.pooling_type`, a file under 1 MiB, a split model's parts summed. A failing model is listed in the log and in the row's help as "Not usable: <name>: <reason>"; the VRAM estimate (file plus the tier headroom) is in the help; a model needing more than the card's total memory (from `--list-devices` after the first start, else one `nvidia-smi` call at most once a minute) is listed as "too large for this graphics card" and never chosen. Listing: ids `custom:<file name>`, after the built-in ones, "(custom)" label. Auto: custom models only with `"auto": true` (then they compete by size; equal sizes keep the built-in first); with Mature content on, a custom model joins the uncensored group only with both `uncensored` and `auto` true (decision for the user to confirm: the spec said both that `uncensored` makes a model eligible for Mature Auto and that custom models are used by Auto only with `auto: true`; the stricter reading is built). A pin always works if it fits. The server starts a custom model with its `contextSize` and `--chat-template`, otherwise the same flags; one that fails to start or dies while warming up is marked broken (until its file changes or reset) and the start is repeated with Auto's choice, with one `local-model-fallback` notice whose text now also says "or did not start" (all 15 locales updated). `allowanceFor(name, {uncensored, family})` honours the manifest flag in both directions instead of the file name. Docs: `docs/LOCAL_AI.md` "Add your own model" (and the developer notes), a short note in `packaging/PLAYER_README.md`. Added `bridge/custom-models.mjs` to the bridge allowlists (`packaging/runtime-layout.mjs`, `packaging/release-plan.json`). Tests: `custom-models.test.mjs`, `custom-model-choice.test.mjs`, the custom block in `local-llm-server.test.mjs`, a custom-row test in `manager.test.mjs`, `mistral-key.test.mjs`; fixture `FAKE_LLAMA_EXIT_FOR_MODEL`. Limits, documented: llama.cpp support for the architecture and a chat template are not checked ahead; an embedding model whose header gives neither away passes and then fails at start (the fallback covers it). **Live check (user, needs the game and a GPU):** add one small instruct GGUF with a manifest, see it in the row marked "(custom)", pin it, Apply, talk; then try an embedding model and a garbage file and read the "Not usable" line in the help.

(1) The odd reply to "what are some of the services you excel at specifically": no stale or mismatched reply (the final text and memory were right, one LLM stage set, and tests across decision waits of 0, 40, 150 and 600 ms show the voice never hears the speculative reply). Root cause: the Portuguese LEAVE stem `some` in `bridge/text-action-words.mjs` matched the English word "some", so the screen found one action and `guess` speculated a reply written under "V sends you away"; the decision then disagreed, the reply was aborted and rewritten (about 1.5 to 2 s and a wasted Mistral request). Fixes: the stem now needs a Portuguese context (`some` at the end, `por favor`, `daqui`, `já`, `de aqui`, `da minha`); `guess` in `bridge/text-actions.mjs` answers NONE (no speculation on an action) for an open question (what, who, why, how...) that is not a request, and for plain remarks about oneself or a third party that do not address her; requests such as "Take the wheel, I'm wiped" still speculate. The coy tone is the model answering in persona; the notes block was left unchanged on purpose. (2) The second message got no reply: probe.log shows `Composer opened` for generations 12 and 13 and no `Native input captured`. Proven: there is no automatic reopen, and Lua never saw a submission; the boxes closed after about 1 to 3 s (Esc, an Enter on an empty box, or an engine close) and the old code dropped all of those silently. The exact trigger is not provable from the logs, so the box now reports how it ended: `Composer.reds` stores `m_convaiCloseInfo` (nodata, confirm, empty, closed:N) read through `ConvaiComposerClosedInfo()`; `mod/init.lua` (`convaiComposerWatch`) writes one probe.log line `Composer closed without a message: generation=N result=... open=Ns` and posts the new notice `message-lost` ("Your message was not sent. Open the text box again and retype it.", repeat 5 s, 15 locales, `docs/NOTIFICATIONS.md`) for an empty Enter or a close without a result (Esc stays quiet). Other silent drops now log `Message lost: ...` and post the notice too: `sendRequest` returned false, late input after the target was gone, a failed take. No per-frame work (runs on box open and close only). Install: `mod/init.lua`, `mod/notices.lua`, `mod/locales/*.lua` (CET reload); `bridge/text-action-words.mjs`, `bridge/text-actions.mjs` (bridge restart); `r6/scripts/CyberpunkConvai/Composer.reds` (GAME RESTART; until then the Lua logs `result=unknown` and posts nothing it cannot be sure of). **2026-10-13 (branch `crouch-sync`; unit-tested; NOT installed, NOT seen in the game, game not touched): companion crouch syncing.** Live bug (Carol Emeka, probe.log 09:48Z): she did not crouch at first, then crouched, and stayed crouched after V stood. Read from the log: `crouch` 09:48:11, an idle flavour gesture began 09:48:25 while she was meant to be crouched, `stand - workspot` 09:48:26, `crouch` 09:48:28, gesture `exit not relaxed` 09:48:29, `stand` 09:48:36 (logged, no visible effect). Causes found in code: (1) idle and talk gestures never looked at the crouch, so the workspot started over the pose and the stance module took the pose apart (stand, then crouch) while the workspot was still ending; (2) a stand was fire-and-forget: `NPCPuppet.ChangeStanceState` returns nothing and returns early when the blackboard already matches, so an ignored stand was never noticed, while a crouch was already read back and retried; (3) V crouching again while a stand was unconfirmed left her crouched with no record, so the next stand never came. The trigger is an event (`PlayerPuppet.OnLocomotionStateChanged`) applied at the next 10 Hz tick (at most 0.1 s) or, when a blocker holds her, at the next 0.5 s re-check; the code does not explain a visible delay and the stuck pose is not proven to come from the stance (see open question). Fix: `companions.lua` passes `crouched` to the gesture owner; `companion-gestures.lua` starts nothing while it is set and leaves at once (`exit` reason `crouching`); `companion-stance.lua` reads every stand back (re-issues up to three times while the stance reads Crouch, then `stand not kept by the game`), adopts a still-present crouch when V crouches again, exposes `holds(serial)`, logs `crouch waiting - <reason>` once per reason when a blocker holds her, and adds `hls=<high-level state>` to the crouch, stand and not-kept lines. Open question for the next live test: if `hls` is not Relaxed after a crouch or stand, the visible pose comes from the high-level state (Alerted or Stealth locomotion wrapper) and the next step is to restore Relaxed; if `hls` is Relaxed and the stance reads Stand but she looks crouched, the animation graph does not re-read the stance while she idles. What limits quality:
- **Asterisks:** `cleanReply` deletes the word inside asterisk emphasis, which hits 15 to 30 percent of replies.
- **Builder bridge:** sample echoes, tone angles that pull off voice, metres given on every shot, and raw keys like `firstBlood` that leak into lines.
- **No length cap:** a third of lines go over the word limit.

ministral 14B: the built-in judge scores it higher and it drops fewer repeats, but the blind judge rates it the same as 8B.

Now a turn never waits for the embedder to start (it is started for the next turn, deferred past the request), the server starts with `-fit off` (6.3-7.7 s to 2.6-3.4 s) and stays up 5 minutes: measured 404/408 ms to 2/1 ms on cold turns. The "thinking" status write no longer holds up the request. Queued with exact proposals for the agents in those files: streaming the voice-key reply (0.17-1.2 s), the OmniVoice first phrase (2.36 s: store beside the analysis, a shorter first phrase, a faster kernel, a provisional face), waking the playback pump on the game's lease, publishing before the face write, a cached speech-state read, Mistral connection reuse, `-fit off` for the chat server. **2026-10-13: the Local AI prompt is fitted to the server's context, a turn it cannot answer goes to the cloud or says so (unit-tested and run against the fake llama-server; NOT yet seen in the game).** Live record 2026-10-12: the player talked to Judy and heard nothing; `The local AI request (8790 tokens) exceeds the available context size (8192 tokens)`. Root cause: the server ran at a fixed 8,192 tokens while the prompt was bounded only in characters (persona and rules about 4.5k tokens, the rest up to 9k+), and the refusal was a code-less, non-retried, non-falling-back error. Fix: `bridge/prompt-budget.mjs` fits every Local and Groq (8,000 tokens a minute) request to n_ctx minus a reply reserve, estimated with a learned ratio and counted with `/tokenize` near the limit, cutting jobs, journal history, recent events, gear, retrieved memories, older turns, the summary, the tracked quest and the world facts in that order (discrete cuts, so the prefix cache holds) and never the persona, rules, right-now block or the player's words; a refusal that still comes is learned from and retried once. Context per tier: the supervisor asks for 16,384, then 12,288, then 8,192 by free video memory and reads the real n_ctx from `/props`; measured +136 MiB (standard, 3,008 to 3,144 MiB) and +104 MiB (lite, 1,399 to 1,503 MiB) from 8k to 16k, q8_0 KV saves only 75 to 90 MiB and is not used. A failed local turn falls back to Mistral (key saved) or Groq, with the notice `local-turn-fallback`; with no cloud provider the game says `local-failed`. EPERM on `knowledge-status.json`: a reader without the delete share (CET `io.open` in the Lua heartbeat check) blocks the rename; the bridge's retry already outlasts it, the log line is now rate-limited, the plugin needs no change. **2026-10-13: companion actions now work on the Mistral and Local AI text paths (unit-tested and measured against the real Mistral API; NOT yet seen in the game: needs a bridge restart and a CET reload; Gemma measured only in part).** Root cause of Judy ignoring "drive for me": the text path never read `config.companionAction` at all (no action prompt, no parser, no delivery), so only Convai could act, and the replies were pure talk. Convai's actions are drive to the waypoint, attack the marked target, follow, and leave the party; there is no wait, stay, sit or stop action in the game. Design (`bridge/text-actions.mjs`, wired in `TextProviderHost`): a separate 12-token classifier request (one word, temperature 0, runs beside the memory lookup, failure means plain talk) decides, the reply prompt gets a `GAME ACTIONS` note in the volatile block (stable prefix untouched) that says what is asked or what V has to do first, and the host delivers the same message Convai would send after a good reply; stray `[CODE]` tags are stripped before the voice. New `driveUnavailable` code (Lua `gameplay-actions.lua` -> `protocol.mjs` -> `companion-actions.mjs`, text routes only) carries why a ride is impossible. Rejected: tool calls (ministral-8b returns no speech on action turns and picks the wrong tool) and a code at the start of the reply (recall 12% or precision 58%). Eval (`scripts/Eval-MistralPrompt.mjs --actions`, ministral-8b, 6 characters, 27 situations, n=3): before 0 of 196 asked actions fired; after precision 100% (195/195), recall 99% (195/197), 0 false triggers in 288 turns; a Haiku judge scored false promises on impossible requests 19% before and 3% after, and replies that name what is needed 12% before and 26% after (wait and sit still draw a promise 17% and 6% of the time). Gemma 4 E4B through the same classifier (own llama-server, 2 characters, 16 situations, n=2, 64 replies; it takes about 7 s a reply on this GPU): precision 100% (13/13), recall 81% (13/16: one follow and two leaves missed, so a miss means V repeats the request); before is 0 by construction. Open: watch the first live "drive for me" with a car, a waypoint and V on foot; add a local-model eval cell for multi-turn history.

**2026-10-13: Convai sign-in backend built on branch `convai-auth`, nothing deployed, bridge mode OFF by default (unit-tested only; no live Convai, Vercel or Upstash call was made).** Design: `docs/CONVAI_AUTH_BACKEND.md`. Backend: `auth-backend/` (Vercel Node functions: `POST /api/convai/token`, `GET /api/admin/turns`, `/api/healthz`, `/api/readyz`; no dependencies). Every limit is one Redis script call (one Upstash command per token request): per-install and per-address hourly limits, new installs per address per day, a global daily mint cap ("busy"), a server-side turn backstop (an install whose reported UTC-day turns reach 100 gets no new token, "daily limit reached"), kill switch, minimum mod version, blocklist, signed requests (HMAC plus a +-120 s timestamp; obfuscation only, the secret ships in the bridge), fail closed when Redis is down. Two modes behind `CONVAI_AUTH_MODE`: `shared` (default, one token per warm instance) and `per-install` (own token per install, revoked on the cap; needs a live test because Convai's mint limit is unpublished). Bridge: `bridge/convai-credential.mjs` (`TokenSource`: fetches in the background at start, renews 8 to 10 minutes before expiry, never on a turn; install id in `runtime/convai-install.json`), `ConvaiKeys.credentialFor`, `RealtimeHost` `credential` hook, `realtime-client.mjs` passes `authToken`, `player-memory-api.mjs` backend mode (API-AUTH-TOKEN header, no character list/read/update), `scripts/Enable-CharacterMemory.mjs` (developer-side, NOT run). Switch on with `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_AUTH_BACKEND=1`, `..._AUTH_URL`, `..._AUTH_SECRET` (or `runtime/convai-auth.json`); `..._AUTH_FALLBACK=0` removes the embedded-key fallback (default on; logged only in bridge.stderr.log; only used when the backend is unreachable, never when it refuses). A player's own key is untouched. Open: deploy steps are in `auth-backend/README.md` (CLI-driven); step 0 of the design doc (token on memory calls, revoke shape, mint limit) still needs one live check; a release step must write `convai-auth.json` with the signing secret into the package; run `Enable-CharacterMemory.mjs --apply` before players use backend mode.
