**2026-10-13 (late): four live findings on the native core, fixed in branch `native-core` (DLL `7442124bd33c...`, plus CET reload; NOT yet proven in game).** (1) `vehicles=lua (mounting keeps answering unavailable)`: `GetMountingFacility`, `GetMappinSystem`, `GetScriptableSystemsContainer` (and `GetSceneSystem`, used by `faces`) are NOT global functions. Parsing `r6/cache/final.redscripts` (the format: header, six tables; names, name offsets, definitions of 20 bytes) shows each as a native static function of the script class `GameInstance` (native `ScriptGameInstance`) with one parameter `self`; the only globals that take a `GameInstance` are `GetPlayer`, `GetMainPlayer` and `GetPlayerObject`. The old lookup searched the globals only. `convai::game::GameSystem` now looks in the statics of `ScriptGameInstance` / `GameInstance`, then the globals, then all class functions, and else asks the instance's own system lookup for the native class; the route is logged (`Game access: GameInstance.GetMountingFacility resolved as ... (static function of class ScriptGameInstance)`). (2) `NPCPuppet.IsInCombat not found`: the game registers the static as `IsInCombat;ScriptedPuppet` on `NPCPuppet` itself (the compiler appends parameter types after a `;`; PlayerPuppet's member is `IsInCombat;`), so `GetFunction("IsInCombat")` finds nothing; the earlier claim that it lives on `ScriptedPuppet` was wrong (that is its parameter type). One matcher (`ScriptNameIs`, headless-tested) now serves `game::Method`, `game::StaticFunction`, `FindMember` and `vreflect::StaticFunction`, so the actuator and faces read the combat flag natively and the chauffeur's `P` section and `ProbeJson` get `IsInCombat` too; faces' `GetSceneSystem;GameInstance` global (also not a global) goes through `GameSystem`. The parity gate compares the combat field (new counters, proof needs it compared on every counted sense, `PARITY MISMATCH in combat`, proven line says who reads it). (3) Judy in a car: `seated-look-skip {"reason":"in a vehicle"}` is V's own camera widening (`mod/seated-look.lua`), not her gaze; her gaze has its own gates and none of them was logged, so the cause is not provable offline (the Oct 2 live pass used the same Lua with narrower limits). Changes: a `Companion recovery seated-gaze {...}` probe line when her seated attention changes (selected, gate, style, speed, error), seated limits widened (full 100/150/150, narrow 60/120/150; V is about 90 degrees off a passenger's axis, where the old 70/120 faded the look to about 60 percent), `calculatePositionInParentSpace` set for seated requests (as the game's in-vehicle look-at does), and speed bands (full to 8 m/s, narrow to 20, none above, 2 m/s margins). (4) `companions.update` 6.3 to 10.6 ms/s: from the perf snapshots the jump is Judy appearing (3 ms/s before her, 12.8 in the parity window, 12.6 proven, no drop after the proof at 21:03:28Z), and FPS drives the row (7.4 ms/s at 40-50 FPS, 14.5 below 30); proven native vs plain Lua is not separable from that data (other native systems differed between the sessions; matched-FPS rows showed proven native 1.5-2 ms/s higher, not a controlled comparison). Fixes: the combat read no longer falls back to Lua every tick, the window after the first 40 senses narrows to one sense in four while only walking is missing (a standing companion used to hold it open at twice the cost), and perf rows `tickNative.life/sense/commandState` make the A/B possible. Tests: ctest 64 + plugin_host (new: script names, seated plan), node 431 on the native, gaze, vehicle, chauffeur, passage and companion shims (new: combat proof, sparse window, seated bands, seated-gaze probe line). Detail: `docs/NATIVE_VEHICLES.md`, `docs/NATIVE_ACTUATOR.md`, `docs/COMPANION_GAZE.md`.

**2026-10-13: vehicle group merged onto the current `native-core`; names audited against the game (one DLL now carries every system; NOT live).** Registration: the three classes use `StaticClass(name, system)` and plain `Static()` calls, so `rtti::CommitAll` checks every parameter and return type (`String`, `Bool`, `Int32`, `Double`, `handle:gameObject`, `handle:IScriptable`; no `array:Double`) and trips a system whole when one is missing; the per-class `TypesExist` helpers are gone. Names checked against the RED4ext SDK headers (native `NAME` against script `ALIAS`) and the strings of `r6/cache/final.redscripts`: the enums `gamePSMVehicle`, `gamedataVehicleType`, `gameAutodriveDestinationType`, `gameAutodriveLaneValidityResult` and the struct `gamemountingMountingInfo` are the native names; `NPCPuppet`, `PlayerPuppet`, `AutoDriveSystem`, `AIVehicleCommand` and `AIVehicleDriveToPointAutonomousCommand` have no alias; `DynamicEntitySystem.IsReady/IsManaged/IsTagged` are Codeware natives. Two real bugs found by that audit, both fixed: (1) `CClass::GetFunction(shortName)` answers the first function of that name, statics before members, so overloads such as `IsAttached`/`IsVehicle`/`IsDestroyed`/`IsInCombat` (member and static versions under one short name) can resolve to a function with other parameters; this is also why the live actuator logged `NPCPuppet.IsInCombat is not a one-argument static function` (the nearest `IsInCombat` is a member, the static `IsInCombat(puppet)` is declared on `ScriptedPuppet`). The vehicle group now resolves members by name AND parameter count (`vreflect::FindMember`, nearest class first, statics skipped), statics from the nearest declaring class (`StaticFunction`), refuses an argument list that does not fill the parameters, caches only hits and logs what the class does have on a miss. NOT applied to the actuator (`ActuatorGame.cpp` `CombatFunction` still uses `GetFunction`): the same fix would let the plugin read the combat flag there. (2) The three global functions (`GetMountingFacility`, `GetMappinSystem`, `GetScriptableSystemsContainer`) are tried as `<name>;GameInstance` and then by short name with one `ScriptGameInstance` parameter among all global functions; the resolved name is logged. Shims: passage's self-test wait no longer fails after five waits (same rule as clearance: wait, retry every 2 s then 10 s); all three honour `runtime/native-verify.txt` (`api.verifying`); every doc and comment names only the file switches. Tests: node 21 (vehicles), 18 (passage) and 28 (chauffeur) shim tests (new: native-verify.txt in each, passage waits, a source contract on the vehicle group), ctest 61 + plugin_host.

**2026-10-11: daily cap and abuse protection for the project's shared Convai key (built and unit-tested; NOT live: bridge restart plus CET reload for the Lua and locale files; the dev checkout is not limited, see below).** Turns on the packaged key are limited to 100 per local calendar day (`DAILY_LIMIT`), counted once per turn at the single choke point where turns reach Convai (`RealtimeHost`: typed, spoken, Phone Chat, each group speaker, look-ahead turns and automatic reactions; a microphone turn is checked at its start and counted at its finish; connection opens and warm-ups are not counted). A token bucket (15 at once, 12 a minute) and 250 ms spacing apply on top. The count is kept in two HMAC-signed copies (`daily-usage.json` in the state folder and under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CyberpunkConvai`), so deleting one does not reset it; a damaged or edited copy is ignored and never blocks the player (count 0, rate limit still on). At the cap the bridge refuses the turn before any connection is opened (`[convai-quota:daily]`, reply code `daily-limit`); the game shows one `daily-limit` notice per session (Convai key recommended, or a free Mistral key, Settings > Development) and Phone Chat words it on its status row; battle and loot reactions stop silently. Settings > Development shows "The shared plan: N of 100 left today" and the sidebar of "Use my own Convai API key" explains both free options. A player's own Convai key and other providers are never counted or limited. The package key is now stored scrambled (`convai-key-v1`, `bridge/key-codec.mjs`; the release build round-trip-checks it) and only a packed key is treated as the shared one, so a plain `runtime/convai-key.txt` (development) and a player's own `convai-key.txt` are unlimited. To test the limit with a dev key: `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_DAILY_LIMIT=3`; `off` or `0` disables it; the packaged launcher strips the variable. Honest limits: the bridge ships as readable source and the key ships inside the package, so editing the code, deobfuscating the key or deleting both counter copies is not stopped; there is no port that accepts turns (file mailbox in the game folder), so no token was added. Tests: `bridge/shared-key-guard.test.mjs`, extended manager, phone-chat, supervisor and packaging tests.

**2026-10-11: Local speech-to-text for the voice key on the Mistral route (bridge + packaging; BRIDGE RESTART; UNVERIFIED in game; `docs/LOCAL_STT.md`).** Moonshine Tiny English int8 (MIT, 27 M parameters) run by sherpa-onnx 1.13.6 (Apache-2.0) on the CPU, in the Pocket Python. Chosen by measurement on 26 clips / 130 s (game actors, LibriSpeech, Windows voices with game names): WER 11.4-11.7%, final decode p50 0.18 s / p95 0.28 s on 2 threads and 0.45 / 0.67 s on 1, against faster-whisper tiny.en 12.0% at 0.82 s, base.en 10.4% at 1.9 s, small.en 7.6% at 8 s, a streaming Zipformer 12.7% (game 28%) and Moonshine Base with no gain for 3x the size. Default is ONE thread (onnxruntime pools spin-wait: 2 threads cost 3x the CPU for 30% less time), below-normal priority, live words from a decode of the newest 8 s every 1.2 s at about 15% duty, and a live decode that already covered the recording is reused as the final text (about 3 ms). No process runs outside a recording; the worker quits after 90 s idle. Audio: `bridge/local-stt-capture.mjs` opens a 16 kHz mono AudioWorklet in the hidden Chrome (served from memory, mic granted per context), 100 ms Int16 chunks to the bridge; the existing `MicrophoneSession` states, notices, 700 ms minimum, spam handling and `microphone-heard.json` words run unchanged, and an empty transcript becomes the existing no-speech notice. Wired as `mistralSpeech` in `convai-bridge.mjs` (`createLocalSpeech`); the Convai route never starts it. Model in the HF bucket `final/stt-model/moonshine-tiny-en-int8/` (124 MB, manifest updated by `scripts/Upload-SttModel.py`), `release.config.json` group, `models/stt` in the package, wheels in `pocket.lock.txt`, notices, closure lists, install test transcribes the Pocket sentence. Tests: `local-stt.test.mjs` (16) and `local-stt-capture.test.mjs` (12, includes Chrome's fake mic through the real worker); bench: `node scripts/Bench-LocalStt.mjs --synth --live`. Live check: Provider Mistral, press the voice key, say a sentence with a name, press again: the words show while speaking and the reply follows; silence gives the no-speech notice.

**2026-10-11: V no longer keeps walking after the talk box: the box waits until no movement key is held (redscript; GAME RESTART, plus CET reload for the Lua half; UNVERIFIED live).** Cause (user confirmed it is the text talk box, not the phone): a movement key released while the Codeware popup owns input never reaches gameplay, so the axis still reads held after the box closes and V walks on until the key is pressed again. No retail API to release input was found (and none is used), so the fix keeps the key-up from being lost: `Composer.reds` `ConvaiMoveWatch` is registered on the player from `OnGameAttached` (removed in `OnDetach`) for exactly two actions, `MoveX` and `MoveY` (`r6/config/inputContexts.xml` MovementActions: A/D and W/S plus the left stick). The game calls it only when an axis value changes, it stores the two values (held = either above 0.15) and consumes nothing, so there is no per-frame work. `init.lua`: the talk hotkeys (F6/F7 and the group one) ask `player:ConvaiMoveHeld()`; if a direction is held, the box is not opened but the request waits (`convaiTalkGate`, serviced from onUpdate only while a request waits) until the axis is released, at most 1.5 s. At the cap the box opens anyway (chosen over a hint or a refusal: a talk request is never dropped, and no new localised text is needed), the stuck reading is forgotten (`ConvaiMoveForget`) so the next press is not delayed, and in that one case a key released inside the box can still be lost (known issue stays in `packaging/PLAYER_README.md` until verified). A second press while waiting only changes private/group; the wait is dropped on menu, pause or world change. `Composer opened:` log line keeps `speed=` and adds `moveAxis=held|free|n/a` (n/a = redscript tracker not installed, the box then opens at once) and `waited=` when it waited; `Talk box waits for the movement keys to be released` is logged when a press is deferred. Tests: `phone-input.test.mjs` (tracker shape and the two named registrations, Lua gate: immediate open, wait then open once, cap with forget, second press, world drop). Live check: hold D, press the talk hotkey, release D: the box opens at once on release (probe.log `moveAxis=free waited=0.xx`); hold D past 1.5 s and the box opens anyway; walk with D, tap the hotkey after releasing, type, close the box, V must stand still. If the tracker shows `moveAxis=held` while standing, a key-up was missed earlier (menu, vehicle): the next press waits 1.5 s once and clears it.

**2026-10-11: a locked state file no longer stalls companion preparation (bridge; restart the bridge).** Report: "Alex could not prepare: Companion preparation is not responding" with `bridge.stderr.log` lines `Preparation poll: EPERM: operation not permitted, rename '...companion-invitations-state.json.<uuid>.tmp'` between 14:40 and 14:48 IST. Cause: `guarded-file.mjs` `atomicFile` (the shared writer of every game-facing state file) retried the rename only 5 times over 80 ms; when the game's Lua reader or an indexer held `companion-invitations-state.json` longer, it threw, `CompanionInvitations.publishSnapshot` passed the error up, and `pollPrefetch` aborted before it ran the rest of the poll, so the receipt aged out and `invitation-readiness.lua` gave up after 15 s. (`memory.prepareCharacter` itself writes nothing, so it is not involved; the two orphan `.tmp` files in the game runtime folder were from 5 and 10 Oct and are deleted.) Fix: `atomicFile` now tries the rename 6 times with a 10/20/40/80/150 ms backoff (about 300 ms), retries EPERM, EACCES and EBUSY, keeps the old file and removes its temp file (with `rm` retries) when it still fails; `publishSnapshot` catches a failed or throwing write, returns false and counts it (`publishFailures`, `lastPublishError` in the invitation diagnostic), so the poll goes on and the next one writes the fresh receipt. Tests: `guarded-file` (EPERM twice then success, always failing keeps the old file and leaves no temp, default backoff timing), `companion-invitations` (poll survives failed and throwing writes, keeps its stage and writes again). Not changed: private registry writes (`player-memory.json`, `knowledge-service`) have their own writers and are not read by the game.

[Alex=memory]` and at 09:11:00Z / 09:11:21Z `Alex could not prepare: Companion preparation is not responding` (`invitation-readiness.lua`: the bridge receipt did not move past the `memory` stage within 15 s). **2026-10-11: typing no longer swallows key-ups; talk box and phone typing leave speed evidence in probe.log (`PhoneChat.reds` = GAME RESTART; `mod/phone-input.lua`, `mod/phone-chat.lua`, `mod/init.lua` = CET reload).** Bug (live): after typing to an NPC V kept strafing right until D was pressed once. (1) Our phone-typing guards consumed presses AND releases (`PhoneChat.reds` `OnAction`/`OnHandleMenuInput`, `mod/phone-input.lua` overrides on `gameuiInGameMenuGameController`). Now every press is still consumed, but a release is consumed only when it is one of the menu actions that controller acts on (verified in `vendor/reference-game-scripts`: `RegisterInputListenersForPlayer` lists OpenPauseMenu, OpenMapMenu, OpenCraftingMenu, OpenJournalMenu, OpenPerksMenu, OpenInventoryMenu, OpenHubMenu, QuickSave, QuickLoad, FastForward_Hold; the pointer callback is `OnPostOnRelease`, so every event there is a key-up and only back/toggle_* are swallowed; the phone popup keeps cancel, phone_open_journal, up_button, down_button, click). A blanket pass-through of releases was NOT used: the in-game controller opens the pause menu and journal ON RELEASE, so Esc/J would open menus while typing. Honest limit: those two controllers only register menu actions, so they never saw D at all; this part is a guard, and the likelier cause is (2). (2) The talk box (Codeware `GenericMessageNotification.ShowInput`) switches the input context, so gameplay can miss a key-up that happens while it owns input. (3) Evidence: `Composer opened: ... speed=<m/s>` (`mod/init.lua`, one `GetVelocity` read per open) and `Phone chat typing opened: contact=... speed=...` (rising edge inside the existing 10 Hz phone tick, only while a chat is open). **2026-10-11 (voice key: a recording that held no speech waited 60 s and then blamed the microphone; the key is now spam-safe; Lua + bridge; CET reload and bridge restart; no voice build).** Live report: voice input did not work, maybe because the key was spammed. Evidence: the bridge log had `Microphone: ... Convai did not finish the reply` at 12:54:24 (the 60 s reply ceiling in `realtime-client.mjs` `collect`), the Windows microphone consent store showed the bridge's browser held the microphone 12:53:19 to 12:53:24 (device, permission, volume 100 percent and unmuted all fine, default input Realtek array), and `microphone-command.json` held the game's `cancel` written at 12:54:25 by the `error` state. So one 5 s recording was captured, Convai returned no transcript and no reply, the player waited 60 s and saw "Microphone unavailable. Check your Windows input device." Spamming made it likelier: a press while the device was still opening sent `finish` at once and a double tap right after Listening submitted a near-empty recording. Fix: `microphone.lua` `press()` ignores a press while connecting (re-shows the connecting notice), within 0.7 s of Listening (bounce) and while a reply is on its way, finishes otherwise, and an overdue reply (8 s) is dropped by the next press, which begins a fresh recording (`toggleVoice` in `init.lua`, nothing per frame). Bridge: `MicrophoneSession` holds a finish that arrives under 700 ms after the device opened; `collect` fails a voice turn with no transcript, no reply text and no thinking 15 s after the finish as "No speech was heard" (new `no-speech` state, notice `mic-no-speech`, 15 locales translated by a Haiku batch), and the 60 s timeout message now says what had arrived (transcript, text, complete, thinking, audio). Tests: microphone-session 26, microphone-adapter 8, realtime-client 82, plus the knowledge-integration and world-lifecycle hotkey tests now press finish after Listening. **2026-10-10 (night): the shut mouth: our speech was only added to the facial idle (fixed in the graph archive and the writer, built offline; archive NOT installed: game restart with the archive and `FaceFeature.reds`; Lua hot).** Mechanism: every face graph ends in one Sermo solver whose input is the whole pose, and that pose always contains a facial idle (the Idle state machine plays a looped `idle__<emotion>__<sex>` clip, 39 such clips in `woman_average_sermo`; a workspot, a scene or a look-at streams its own on top). The solver (reconstruction in `vendor/reference-cp77-blender/.../facial/solver.py`) multiplies each control by `lerp(1, <control>AnimOverrideWeight, lipSyncEnvelope)`, skipped when the envelope is 0, then adds `<control>LipsyncPoseOutput`. We wrote only the pose tracks (envelope 0, overrides 1), so a jaw of .1 to .65 was added to an idle holding `lips_together` at .7 to 1.0, `jaw_mid_close`, `lips_suck_dn` and purse at that moment; the clip loops, so the seal comes and goes (it showed under gestures because the talk workspots named `interested`, which holds the lips doubly; the neutral idle only lowered it). The gesture agent's idea (override = 1 minus each control's own pose) would not have cured it: a control at 0 for the instant (lips together on a vowel) keeps the idle's closure. Fix: one new float input `speech_owner` (`assets/facial/controls.json` `owner`, 49 nodes per graph from `scripts/Build-FacialGraphs.mjs`) adds to `lipSyncEnvelope` and subtracts from the override weight of the 48 jaw, lip and cheek controls, so 0 is the old graph and 1 removes the idle from the mouth; eyes, brows and lids have no override track and stay untouched, so blinks and emotions are unchanged. `mod/facial-playback.lua` writes it eased in over .1 s while a reply is heard, with the release ease, and 0 when blocked or handed back to the idle writer; an install without the field keeps the old behavior. `face.expressions.lastSpeech.ownedFrames` reports it. Build: the first build failed in WolvenKit (a handle referenced before its definition in document order; the builder now defines the shared input in the outermost node, with a test); second build passed the 9-graph binary round trip (59 deltas, 49 ownership nodes, 60 inputs each) and the 9-entry archive check. Tests: `bridge/facial-graphs.test.mjs` (12), `bridge/companion-expression-playback.test.mjs` (a heard reply owns the mouth, hands it back, older feature without the field). Not done: no live sample (the user was in game with a second probing agent; a probe round was asked to stop), so the engine's use of the override stage is unproven and `Subtract` is read as track minus input; the packaging copy of the archive is not updated; I did not correlate failing moments with workspot enter and exit times (the logs only hold `lastSpeech` totals).

LTM speaker limit reached` at `ConvaiClient.connect`. The free plan allows ONE long-term-memory speaker (`ltm_speaker_limit` 1 in the plan table) and counts every speaker the account was active with in the last 30 days; the mod sends one end-user id per install on every conversation, so an account that had already used memory had no room for it. Now: `speaker` is its own kind and never "limit used up"; on a player's key the refused turn is repeated once without the end-user id and the key's conversations go on without long-term memory (no memory, and no offered companion actions, which need an identified session); one `key-memory` notice with the first such reply, settings line "Your own key, without memory"; if the anonymous request is refused too (`Missing end_user_id`, depends on each character's memory mode, unverified) the notice says to free a memory user or use another key. Unverified until a real free key is used again: that the anonymous request is accepted (the log line `The key's plan has no room for another memory user` and a reply confirm it).

**2026-10-10: a slow OmniVoice start no longer downgrades the session to Pocket.** Cause (from the morning's `bridge.stderr.log`: weights loaded, then "Local voice startup timed out", then `fallback="Omni worker unavailable"` on every reply): `VOICE_WORKER_LIMITS.startupMs` in `bridge/resident-voice.mjs` was one fixed 180 s limit, a start takes about 3 minutes on a CPU-throttled laptop in Windows Silent mode even without the game loading beside it, and a failed worker then stayed out of routing for the whole session (`failedBackends` is cleared only when the player chooses the voice again). Fixes: (1) the startup limit is progress-based: any frame or log line from the worker restarts a 300 s stall window, 900 s is the absolute cap, a worker asked to stop while loading gets 60 s (`resident-voice-worker.py` now sends a `loading` frame after the imports, after the model load and after the CUDA graph, same frame type, no protocol change); (2) `VoiceSelection` keeps the fallback (Pocket) but retries OmniVoice in the background after 45 s, 3 min and 10 min (`omniRetry` and `fallback.temporary` in `local-voice-state.json`): due-checked from the existing 500 ms settings poll (no timer, no loop), only with no reply in flight and voice playback on, in a second worker at below-normal priority (`os.setPriority`, raised to normal once ready) beside Pocket (CPU only, no VRAM); when it is ready the next idle poll commits Omni, adopts that worker (no second load) and releases Pocket, never mid-reply; a fourth failure gives up as before; picking another voice, another reference set, a missing pack or shutdown drops the retry or the loading worker; (3) the player sees one notice when Pocket starts serving, "{requested} is not ready yet. Companions are using {voice} for now." (same `voice-fallback` id and 600 s window; new text in all 15 locales and `localization/en.json`), nothing on the way back, and the permanent "is unavailable" text only if the retries run out; the Settings status line says "not ready yet" for the temporary case; the routing log says "Omni still loading (retrying in the background)". Tests: `bridge/resident-voice.test.mjs` (stall window restarts on output, absolute cap, short close while loading, priority), `bridge/voice-selection.test.mjs` (retry timing and back-off, never during a reply, adoption without a second load, drop on voice change or close, a test with the real `ResidentVoice` and fake child processes), `bridge/manager.test.mjs` (notice wording and silent return), `bridge/voice-routing-log.test.mjs`. Docs: `docs/LOCAL_VOICES.md` ("Startup limit, background retry and switch back"), `docs/NOTIFICATIONS.md`. Not touched: Pocket's own 180 s startup limit; the first OmniVoice start at game launch still runs at normal priority. NOT yet live: **bridge restart** (Python worker, `bridge/` and the engine) plus **CET reload** for the two Lua files (`mod/manager.lua`, `mod/mcm.lua`) and the locale files. In-game check: on Silent power mode, launch the game and talk right away; expect either OmniVoice after a wait, or Pocket with the one "not ready yet" notice and OmniVoice back by itself a few minutes later (watch `[OmniRetry]` lines in `runtime/bridge.stderr.log`).

Test in `bridge/jali-face-text.test.mjs` (fails without the change). Measured offline on the three saved phrases: text path now active, jaw differs by only .04 to .07 (the gain is in contact, purse and F/V per `docs/LIPSYNC_IMPROVEMENTS_2026-10-07.md`), analysis time +160 to +340 ms per 4.5 to 5.5 s phrase (about +.2 s before the first phrase is heard; later phrases analyse while the previous one plays). Bridge only, needs a bridge restart; no Lua, no per-frame work. Revert by restoring the one-line guard, or set `CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_FACE_TEXT=off`.

**2026-10-08: Follow-up questions: characters sometimes show interest in V (new setting, off by default)**
- The user wanted conversations to feel two-sided, not as if only V is interested. Like Natural speech the bridge decides the rate (`bridge/follow-up.mjs`, `FollowUp`: warm .45, neutral .35, dry .20, cold .15, never two turns in a row, pity at least once in 5 turns for warm and neutral); the model decides whether and how a pull fits. Log: `[FollowUp] profile= setting= offered= reason= ended-with-question=`.
- Measured with real Convai (`scripts/Probe-FollowUp.mjs`, fresh test identity per run, memories cleared): 288 lines per setting over Judy, Panam, Johnny and a Tyger Claws ganger. Replies that end in a question 7% off, 23% on (Judy 13 to 31%, Panam 8 to 26%, Johnny 3 to 14%, ganger 3 to 22%); a pull in the last two sentences 11% off, 27% on; average length 21.8 to 24.6 words, none over 75. A Sonnet reader judged 86 pulls of 288: 79 specific, 83 in voice, 65 flowing out of the answer. Findings: the Oct 5 `OPEN_QUESTION_POLICY` line ("do not tack a question on") had to be lifted for the offered turn; the paragraph works much better before Natural speech's "keep the same length and content" than after it (16 of 26 against 13 of 41 offered turns pulled), so it sits before the voice notes and the reply-language line stays last; "X, or Y?" closers fell from 43% to 21% of pulls with the final wording. Known weak spots in the doc.

**2026-10-08: A resident on Pocket spoke with a still mouth**
- Evidence: `runtime/speech-state.json` face `error` = "facial-playback.lua:669: Speaker has no prepared owned facial layer" for request `1791445761-7-10041299ULL` (`resident-male`); probe.log "Focus ownership: actor=10041299ULL managed=false", "crowd=true". The bridge side was fine: `continuous-face.json` carried a `local-jali` timeline with the right request, entity and generation.
- Cause: the face layer was companion-only at both ends. Lua `owns()` required `convaiCompanions.owns(actor)`, and natively `ConvaiFaceService` swapped in the ConvaiFace graph only for dynamic entities tagged `CyberpunkConvaiCompanion` (Ready/Apply also required the tag). A crowd NPC's `face_rig` runs the vanilla `*_sermo` graph with no ConvaiFace input, so no Lua change alone could move it. The earlier "lips moved" resident turns (05:42-06:19 UTC, Convai cloud voice) went through the same gate; what moved then was most likely the vanilla look-at reaction or greeting line, which was suppressed from 06:13 (vanilla-reaction hooks).
- Fix (revised the same day for FPS; the first version, `cca9ec7`, prepared every world NPC at `Entity/Initialize` and never shipped): on demand only. `init.lua` calls `NPCPuppet.ConvaiFaceRequest()` for the talk target when a conversation opens. `ConvaiFaceService.RequestWorldFace` checks the running face without writing it, queues the NPC's current appearance name and calls `ScheduleAppearanceChange` with that same name. The existing `Entity/Extract` callback (one size check per build while nothing is pending) prepares that appearance-only rebuild. `ConvaiFaceReady` adopts a world NPC whose running `face_rig` carries our graph, and a dynamic entity still needs the companion tag. At most two world NPCs keep the layer. Lua `speaker()` gates speech playback and `owns()` (companions) gates the idle pass. Isolated redscript compile passes. Unproven in game: whether a same-name appearance change rebuilds `face_rig`, and whether the rebuild is visible.
- Tests: `continuous-speech.test.mjs` (ambient Pocket via `continuous-face.json`, idle pass, unprepared NPC), `facial-playback.test.mjs` (ambient Omni), `facial-graphs.test.mjs` (native contract); the two Lua tests fail on the old `facial-playback.lua`.

**2026-10-08: context emotion selector, neutral rest, Convai's emotion for local voices**
- Cause of Judy's smile on a sad Evelyn question: the Lua resting smile (Judy about .22) plus the text plan's resting Trust (.67 for warm characters) under every sentence; pleasant words (love, family, glad, thanks, beautiful, laughed, V) scored as smiles, so grief told through fond memories smiled harder; only the reply was read, never the question; regret and empathy phrases scored almost nothing. **2026-10-08: Ordinary NPC first-reply latency**
- Report: a generic resident took ~14 s to first audio. `bridge-latency.json`: `memoryAdmissionMs` 6710, `connectionMs` 3909 cold, `firstAudioMs` 3132 (Convai voice).
- Cause 1: `admitPlayerConversation` ran `PlayerMemory.beginConversation` for ambient profiles too; the first turn per profile per bridge run called `enableMemory` (`/character/list` is 2.2 MB, ~2.6 s; `/character/get` ~1 s; update + readback when off). It also turned `resident-male`'s Convai memory on (now true; `resident-female` and `npc-*` still false). Fix: `providerMemory: 'session-only'` on ambient routes (`player-knowledge.mjs`) and `PlayerMemory.beginSessionConversation` (local Forget target only, no provider call).
- Cause 2: an ambient composer hint had no entity, so nothing warmed, and opening the composer again even closed the page the previous turn used (the second turn to the same resident reconnected, 3.7 s). Fix: the talk keys pass the entity (`conversation-prewarm.json` `entity`), Auto-connect publishes `entities` for warmed and partnered characters, and `PartyConnections` warms exact ambient routes (composer, nearby, partner) within the existing caps; the addressed body wins its profile's slot.

**2026-10-07: Convai early audio-player open (latency item A)**
- Where the time went (real Edge, real `realtime-client`, player, worklet, host pump and `ConvaiContinuousSpeech`; fake Convai SDK emitting 24 kHz audio at 2.87x with 100 ms chunks; simulated game finding the reply within 0 to 100 ms like `mod/init.lua`'s 0.1 s poll, then refreshing control every 40 ms; harness is scratch, not committed): the player was created at the first audio packet, and a fresh AudioContext+worklet only starts rendering about 120 to 230 ms after `open()` returns (about 20 ms of `open()` on a warm page, about 190 ms on a page's first context). Control to sound was 120 to 230 ms right after open, but about 30 ms when the context had been running for 300 ms or more. The 400 ms start-up buffer fills in about 105 ms at 2.87x, so it is not the bottleneck.
- Why the old note was too pessimistic: the bridge pump already sends a quiet control every 40 ms while the request is in flight, but a player opened early still must not depend on that (a bridge stall of 2 s would fail a turn that today is harmless), so the early player is not leased at all.
- Design: `ContinuousPcmPlayer.open({standby: true})` opens the device at turn start (`attachContinuous`, so text turns and the microphone finish) in the expected 24 kHz mono. A standby core renders silence, ignores controls and `hold`, rejects audio, and has no lease; it is bounded only by a 70 s ceiling (`PCM_LIMITS.standbyMs`, above the 60 s reply ceiling). `arm()` ends standby and starts the ordinary 2 s lease at that moment (it admits nothing; the game's allowing control still does). The client keeps the standby player separate from `live.player`, so a failed or unusable standby (open error, device change, a source format other than 24 kHz mono) just falls back to opening a player at the first audio as before. Cancel (`close`), a failed text send, a failed microphone finish and the 60 s no-audio timeout all stop it. Game ownership, the lease after the first audio and the Lua side are unchanged.
- Measured (3 interleaved before/after runs, think time 2.3 s, medians of per-run medians, first packet to first rendered samples): warm page 302 to 141 ms, first turn in a page 274 to 135 ms (to device-clock position above zero: 329 to 162 and 306 to 158). **2026-10-08: Natural speech tuned against the real characters**
- The user heard no difference on Pocket or Omni 32. Built `scripts/Probe-NaturalSpeech.mjs` (same context assembly as the bridge, real Convai, throwaway identity, 20 varied prompts, one session per character) and measured about 400 requests: the block does reach the model and Omni over-used it (Judy 85%, Johnny 60%, half as the first word), while the Pocket wording suppressed even natural pauses (5% against 15% with no instructions); the last Apply in the settings file left one Omni turn.
- Fix: the bridge offers the devices on a share of turns by trait (warm .36, neutral .30, dry .22, cold .08; never right after a device; one decision per request) for both engines, with rewritten texts (at most one, where the feeling lands, not a habit to open with). Result in 8 to 12 replies per cell: expressive characters 25 to 33%, Johnny 8 to 17%, archetypes 0 to 13%, no consecutive repeats. New `[NaturalSpeech]` log lines per reply. **2026-10-07: Expressive emotions setting**
- Second setting from the user, off by default. `bridge/expressive-emotions.mjs` holds the tag set (mapped onto the eight emotion families, calm = resting face; subtle .45, `:strong` .8), the per-turn context text and the setting; `bridge/natural-speech.mjs` parses both tag kinds (brackets = voice sounds, braces = feelings) so the display text, Omni's voice text and the marks (`emotionMarks`, character offsets in the clean text) come from one pass. `analyseReply`/`createPlanner` take `marks`: each mark is a forced segment boundary and its feeling holds to the next mark; text before the first mark keeps the text reading, no marks keeps the old plan exactly.
- Timing: no new aligner. The plan's segments now begin at the marks and `expression-timeline.mjs` places them in the audio as it already did (Omni phrase edges exact, then pauses in the mouth timeline, then syllable-proportional estimate), so the face changes when the words are spoken. Mid-sentence marks without a pause are an estimate (about 0.2 s), sentence and phrase starts are anchored to the real silence. Cloud voice switch, locales and tests as for Natural speech (`bridge/expressive-emotions.test.mjs`, three Lua tests, two real-`synthesizeReply` tests).

**2026-10-07: Natural speech setting**

Quest scenes keep combat dialogue as `Vo_Context_Quest`; the only line-level cues are entry-point names (`*_bossfight_in`, `*_low_health_in`) and scene names (`q110_08c_bossfight`, `q108_18b_combat`). Acoustic model: logistic regression on within-voice robust z-scores (loudness, short-term p90, pitch median/p90/range, alpha ratio, spectral tilt, brightness, HNR, rate) trained on the game's own labels (strong source vs ordinary quest dialogue), cross-validated by voice, AUC about 0.78, threshold at 2% of ordinary dialogue; ECAPA distance from the voice's conversational centroid is a small fixed-weight extra; transcript cues add a little; duration is only a tie-break. Mr. Hands and Songbird are two-performer voices (ECAPA 2-means centroid cosine 0.02 and 0.50) and get one baseline per performer; without that 16% of Mr. Hands was falsely flagged. Duration is not needed as a prior (flagged share: under 2.5 s 14%, 2.5-4 s 9%, 4-6.5 s 4%, over 6.5 s 2%); no new length minimum was added (references 1.5-9 s, targets 2.5-6.5 s and 5 words, Adam's picks last 1.9-4.8 s). **2026-10-06 (expressions): why local voices had no visible face, and the fix**
- Root cause: the wiring was fine (rest pose written about 24,000 times; Omni timelines carry `jali-audio-v1` plus `modelExpressions`), but (1) the text cue needed two lexicon hits, so Judy's reply produced no receipt, (2) the resting smile was .025 and idle-only, and (3) the caps were calibrated against a misread game number. The game's lipsync holds a constant per-line mood offset (smile .10 + brows raise .10 in 39% of 6938 lines, frown .20 + brows lower .324 in 20%); our caps and scaling were at or below it.
- Fix: strengths .5/.8/1, caps up/down .20, brow raise .25, lower .32, speech keeps 85%, rest smile .06 in idle and speech, model brow gain .65, and `text-emotion.mjs` now always returns a cue (lexicon, tone, then character warmth; cold characters flat). New per-turn receipts: `runtime/expression-receipt.json` and `speech-state.json` face.expressions.lastSpeech (peak pose). Details in `docs/COMPANION_EXPRESSIONS.md`. Install: `mod/facial-playback.lua` (CET reload) and a bridge restart. Not seen in game yet; if too strong or weak only the numbers change.

**Decisions that stand**
- Voice condition A. No per-character models; one shared model plus a reference per voice, chosen per character by duration (no in-game clip or length setting). Omni stays FP16 (precision test).
- Preserve source audio: no added EQ, pitch, denoise or crossfades.
- Convai speech is one continuous stream; Pocket gets the full reply text once; Omni is phrase-scheduled.
- Shortcuts are the player's own CET bindings. Settings use MCM's own staged Apply (Auto Apply is refused for this provider so drafts stay pending). Esc from the manager returns to gameplay; with unapplied changes the game's OnBack is held and MCM asks first.
- No automatic companion respawn on save load, death, restart or CET reload; fast travel is the exception.
- Lip sync (2026-10-07): per-game model, no per-character models (no reliable gain); trains on ALL lines (shouted and processed lines keep valid curves; voice cloning excludes them); the dialogue text sharpens the mouth when known, with automatic fallback to the audio-only model (`CYBERPUNK_CONVAI_FACE_TEXT=off`).
- Follow-ups are free (no forced questions). Group: the addressed character speaks first; duplicate copies don't multiply speakers.

**Working with the user**
- Ask with a multiple-choice question whenever the user needs to act or decide.
- For tests: launch the game myself (PowerShell `Start-Process` on `bin\x64\Cyberpunk2077.exe`), then give exact steps and observation options, then read the trace.
- Lua changes need CET → Reload All Mods; redscript or plugin changes need a game restart.
- Install by copying only the intended files (from git when other agents have uncommitted work), and compare afterwards.
- Subagents: Sonnet by default, Opus only for genuinely open-ended work. Tell them the same rule for their own helpers.
- Commits: local, focused, no AI attribution, never `git add .`.
